topic_desc_basic: Brahmin are two-headed cattle that serve as a major food source and form of transportation throughout the wasteland, raised for their meat and milk while their waste is used as fertilizer. When utilized by merchants to carry goods, these creatures are known as pack brahmin, and they are a common, non-dangerous sight in settlements like Megaton, Arefu, and the Republic of Dave. In the New California Republic, herding brahmin is a significant industry where wealthy Brahmin Barons influence politicians and laws. Occasionally, a brahmin is born with a single head, a rare mutation referred to as a mono-headed brahmin.

Centaurs are large, fleshy mutated creatures composed of human and canine components, named for their three pairs of leg-like arms. They are commonly found accompanying super mutants, serving as watchdogs and companions to their masters. Centaurs are capable of spitting radioactive projectiles at their targets and possess multiple human arms that they use to drag themselves along the ground. Earlier wasteland accounts describe two-headed centaurs with one canine and one humanoid head, each connected to the body by thick elongated necks, though more recent sightings in the Capital Wasteland describe a single head with three writhing tentacle-like tongues.

Deathclaws are large, highly dangerous mutated predators originally engineered by the pre-war United States government from Jackson's Chameleon stock as replacements for human soldiers in close-combat missions. After the Great War, they spread across North America and established packs led by a pack leader and pack mother, nesting in locations that often disrupt trade routes and make surrounding areas extremely hazardous. They are widely feared as some of the most dangerous creatures in the wasteland, with only behemoths regarded as a greater threat, and some wastelanders who have never encountered them consider them mythical. The Enclave experimented on Deathclaws in several locations, including the creation of Intelligent Deathclaws at Vault 13 through FEV injection, resulting in creatures with increased intelligence who eventually recognized their intended role as expendable soldiers.

Eyebots are small, spherical aerial robots equipped with a loudspeaker and an electrical weapon mounted on the front, along with several long antennas extending from their top and back. They are a familiar sight in the Mojave Wasteland and the Divide, where they hover about broadcasting signals or engaging threats with their built-in tasers. Though individually not very dangerous, eyebots are known to detonate when destroyed, posing a minor hazard to anything nearby. A notable eyebot designated ED-E has gained some recognition among wastelanders, and pre-War popular media even featured an eyebot character named RALPHIE, suggesting these robots were well known to the American public before the Great War.

Feral Ghouls are irradiated humans who have lost their minds to brain degeneration, becoming aggressive and dangerous. They are known by many names, including Mindless Ghouls, Zombies, Crazies, and Post-Necrotic Humans. They emit lethal radiation, prefer dark places, and attack with their hands, though some can still use weapons. Their existence fuels prejudice against all ghouls, as many humans assume every ghoul will eventually turn feral.

The Mister Gutsy is a military combat robot developed by General Atomics International and commissioned by the United States Army before the Great War. It is a dedicated combat variant of the civilian Mister Handy model, and units saw action during the Battle of Anchorage in January 2077. Mister Gutsies are equipped with weapons such as 10mm submachine guns, .44 pistols, plasma weapons, and flamethrowers. General Atomics programmed them to be effective soldiers, but the vague definitions used caused issues with their simulated personality units, giving them the ability to refuse orders from commanders they deemed incompetent or those under court martial.

The Mister Handy is a variant of service and maintenance robot found operating in the Mojave Wasteland. They are equipped with a powerful propulsion system that enables them to hover a few feet above the ground. A Mister Handy features a spherical chassis topped with three optical sensors and three primary appendages for manual labor. Among these appendages are a buzz saw and a rudimentary flamethrower, allowing the robot to perform its duties effectively.

Mole rats are mutated descendants of a species closely resembling a larger variant of heterocephalus glaber, having survived the Great War by burrowing underground where the soil shielded them from direct nuclear blasts. The subsequent radioactive fallout greatly increased their size and aggression, producing the hostile creatures now found throughout the Capital Wasteland and as far afield as Point Lookout. They attack by charging their prey and lunging to bite with their large incisors, though they may retreat if severely outmatched. Despite their aggression, some wastelanders have been known to train and keep mole rats as pets, and raiders have even hosted mole rat races at a dedicated track.

The RobCo Protectron is a sturdy pre-War security automaton used in both private and business sectors across the United States. Powered by a fission battery and featuring three photo sensors for sight, these robots were stored in special pods connected to terminals running the Standard Protectron Control Interface. Their introduction displaced many human workers, leading to violent labor strikes between employees and the machines. Protectrons were manufactured in numerous variants for civil service applications, including firefighter models with cryo guns, medic units with defibrillator hands, police units using shock attacks, construction models with nail guns, and office, utility, and Vault helpers with specialized software.

Radroaches, sometimes called Great American Cockroaches or by their scientific name periplaneta americana, are a common mutated insect species descended from pre-War cockroach populations. They are found throughout the Capital Wasteland and are generally hostile to humans, flapping their wings and antennae before attacking. Their meat is edible, though Moira Brown of Megaton famously describes the taste as resembling old feet. Some radroaches have been observed in unusual circumstances, such as the non-hostile specimens found near the so-called Roach King, or the undersized ones kept as pets by individuals like Gallo in the County Sewer Mainline.

Radscorpions are mutated descendants of the North American Emperor scorpion, enlarged by radiation and Forced Evolutionary Virus exposure following the Great War. They are found throughout the wasteland and are known for their venom, from which antidotes have been derived.

Robobrains are pre-war robots developed by General Atomics International under Doctor Bert Riggs, representing the company's first successful union of organic matter and robotics. Research and production were conducted at facilities operated by General Atomics, RobCo Industries, and the US Army Robotics Division, including Sierra Army Depot and RB-2851. Early models used chimpanzee brains, but the program ultimately sought human brains to augment the robot's functions, accelerate decision-making, and ensure unquestioning obedience. Candidates for brain extraction were drawn from military and civilian prisons, targeting adults of high intelligence and sufficient constitution to survive the removal process.

Sentry Bots are heavy combat robots created to provide security through overwhelming firepower, utilizing a minigun or Gatling Laser on one arm and a Missile Launcher on the other. They possess judicial circuits that allow them to witness crimes such as murder or thievery and hand down death sentences to criminals they identify. A combat inhibitor on their back can cause them to frenzy if damaged, and their fusion core becomes vulnerable during a cooldown phase after attacking. These robots are found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, Big MT, and the Divide, with variants including the Mk series and dedicated Army models.

Super Mutants, sometimes simply called Mutants, are hulking humanoid creatures created by exposing humans to the Forced Evolutionary Virus. They typically possess exceptional strength, endurance, and immunity to radiation and disease, though their intelligence is often modified. Various strains of these mutants exist across the wasteland, originating from places like Mariposa Military Base, Vault 87, the Institute, and West Tek facilities. While many are hostile and obsessively seek out more of the virus, often referred to as "green stuff," to expand their numbers, some groups coexist peacefully with humans.

Abominations are hostile half-human, half-alien hybrids created aboard Mothership Zeta by the alien inhabitants. They possess semi-transparent skin and long arms, attacking intruders without ranged weapons by pointing and wailing before charging to swipe at their targets. Recorded logs indicate that aliens transform humans into these creatures, though not all subjects survive the process. They are found patrolling the ship's hallways or confined in cells, particularly in the Biological Research section of the vessel.

Aliens are hostile extraterrestrial beings encountered aboard Mothership Zeta, commonly seen wearing white spacesuits. They wield advanced weaponry such as Disintegrators, Atomizers, and Shock Batons, and are sometimes protected by an Inertia Suppression Field that functions as a personal shield. Their civilization possesses highly advanced technology, including long-term cryostasis, teleportation, and holograms. A dead alien can also be found far north of the Scrapyard on Earth, alongside an Alien Blaster.

Bloatflies are mutated insects found in the Capital Wasteland, descended from either the common housefly or biting horse fly. The Enclave tentatively classified them within the Tabanidae family, noting that they evolved a unique gland to balance and maintain speed at their enlarged size, though this gland may be toxic if consumed. They attack by launching their own maggots as projectiles and can explode upon death. Bloatflies are known to congregate in areas with available carrion, such as near Reclining Groves Resort Homes where they feed on dead Wastelanders, and within the entrance area of Vault 92.

Experimental Weapons Drones are alien robots encountered on board the alien vessel known as Mothership Zeta. They are used by the aliens for multiple tasks, including combat, personal use, and weapons testing. In the ship's Weapons Lab, two such drones are used to fire at brahmin exiting from a teleportation matrix. All drones aboard the vessel are manufactured at the Robot Assembly.

Fire ants are mutated insects found in the Capital Wasteland, created accidentally by Doctor Lesko through genetic manipulation. The doctor was attempting to return giant ants to their normal size, but a small error in his work produced a different mutation altogether. These creatures breathe fire through a process Lesko calls pyrosis, expelling flammable venom from their venom sacks and igniting it with a spark made by clicking their mandibles. Fire ants employ swarming tactics similar to ordinary giant ants and possess a notable resistance to fire.

Guardian Drones are alien robots used by the aliens aboard Mothership Zeta for a variety of tasks, including combat, personal use, and weapons testing. They are manufactured at the ship's Robot Assembly and can be found stationed throughout the vessel, sometimes resting deactivated within Alien Robot Pods. Each Guardian Drone is equipped with a Drone Cannon, a weapon that fires an arced projectile which rolls along surfaces before exploding. In the Weapons Lab, drones are used to fire at brahmin that emerge from a Teleportation Matrix as part of alien experimentation.

Mirelurks are giant mutated creatures that inhabit the waters and shores of the Capital Wasteland. They are heavily armored, making them difficult to harm, though their faces are a known weak point. Wastelanders such as Grandma Sparkle prize mirelurk meat, especially the softshell variety, as a valuable food source. They appear to require contaminated water to survive, as they begin dying off when exposed to pure water.

Mirelurk Kings are mutated creatures found in the Capital Wasteland. They are known for a ranged sonic attack that can cripple a target's head from afar, though they also possess a more damaging melee attack. Mirelurk Kings cannot attack while swimming and will remain stationary when approached, though their sonic attack can penetrate water. A related variant, the Swamplurk Queen, possesses a spit attack instead of the sonic attack and is more resilient.

Swampfolk are mutated humans inhabiting the Point Lookout swamplands, recognizable by their severe deformities and territorial nature. They mark their territory with hanging dolls and other fetishes, and are known to attack outsiders who wander too close to their grounds. While most Swampfolk are born with their distinctive mutations, rare individuals such as Kenny have been born to Swampfolk parents without deformities and become outcasts as a result. Locals like Marguerite and Haley coexist with or trade alongside the Swampfolk, with Haley noting that they tend to carry a strong smell.

Trogs are mutated humans found in the Pitt, transformed by Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion, a condition caused by the region's concentrated ambient radiation combined with unique industrial toxins and pollutants. The disease is not spread through contact with the infected. Roughly twenty percent of the local populace has undergone the transformation, becoming feral creatures that attack anything on sight, even former friends and loved ones. Children born in the Pitt face a one hundred percent degeneration rate and become feral within weeks of birth.

Yao Guai are mutated bear-like creatures found throughout the Capital Wasteland, typically in craggy, hilly areas or caverns. They are generally encountered in pairs or wandering alone, frequently at night, and are known to inhabit locations such as the Yao Guai Tunnels, Yao Guai Cave, and Cliffside Cavern. Though not as deadly as Deathclaws, Yao Guai are formidable opponents that attack with running pounces followed by slashes and bites. Some wasteland scavengers travel with Yao Guai companions, and these tame specimens will not attack on sight, though they will defend themselves and their ally if threatened.

Bighorners are large herbivorous creatures native to the American Southwest, commonly found in the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon. Humans have domesticated them for their horns, meat, milk, and hides, with settlements such as Goodsprings and Jacobstown keeping herds for survival. Wild bighorners travel in herds of three to seven, often near banana yucca fruit, while domesticated drifts are kept in settlements. They are generally docile but become aggressive if a herd member is distressed or if approached too closely.

Cazadores are large mutated insects created in 2003 at Big MT through DNA splicing experiments conducted in the Z-14 Pepsinae DNA Splicing Lab. Doctor Borous, their creator, denies that they escaped the Big MT crater or are capable of breeding, though both claims are false. In recent years, swarms of cazadores have spread from Big MT into neighboring regions such as the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon. They are most commonly found in mountainous areas, where they build large basket-shaped nests, and they compete with nightstalkers for prey.

Cyberdogs, also spelled cyber dogs, are cybernetically enhanced canines found in Big MT and the Mojave Wasteland, with Antony noting they are an uncommon sight in Denver as well. Notable individual cyberdogs include Rex, who is associated with the King in Freeside, Gabe, and Roxie, a Police Cyberdog created at the X-8 Research Center in Big MT by splicing a robot and a dog together. Despite their mechanical components, cyberdogs are generally considered animals rather than robots. Variants include standard, Police, and Military cyberdogs, with Police and Military variants appearing in Big MT.

Geckos are mutated animals found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, commonly encountered in small packs in areas such as around Goodsprings, along the I-15 toward Primm, and near the Mojave Outpost. Several varieties exist, including the common green gecko, the golden gecko, and the fire gecko, the latter of which is believed to originate from Fire Root Cavern and is capable of breathing fire. A separate population of green geckos is also found in Zion Canyon. Fire geckos are generally hostile to travelers, while other varieties are less aggressive.

Ghost People are mutated inhabitants of the Sierra Madre, transformed by prolonged exposure to the Cloud, a corrosive toxin created at Big MT. They originated as construction workers who were issued bulky hazmat suits to protect against the airborne poison, but the suits' locking mechanisms corroded on contact with the Cloud, trapping the workers inside as the gas slowly changed them. They are the only beings able to move freely through the Cloud, and they gather in hordes beneath the Sierra Madre's streets, hunting in areas thick with the toxic haze such as Salida and Puesta del Sol. Dean Domino questions whether they can even be considered alive, and they are known to carry pressurized gas within their bodies.

Giant mantises are mutated insects found in the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon, originally created by horticultural experiments in Vault 22. They attack by jumping and slicing targets with their forelegs, and can become frenzied if their antennae are damaged. They are commonly encountered near Jacobstown and Spring Mt. Ranch State Park, as well as inside Vault 22 itself.

Lakelurks are mutated aquatic creatures native to the Mojave Wasteland, commonly found around Lake Mead and other watery areas. They are fiercely territorial and aggressive, attacking nearly anything that approaches them or their nests. They typically travel in small groups of two to three, though larger gatherings of five to eight are not uncommon. Lakelurks use sonic pulse shrieks to stun prey from a distance before closing in to tear victims apart with their claws.

Lobotomites are surgically-altered and cybernetically-enhanced humans found at Big MT. Their brains, hearts, and spines were removed and replaced with cybernetics by an Auto-Doc programmed by Doctor Mobius, under the supervision of Doctor Dala. The procedure left them mentally impaired, mute, and hostile to non-Lobotomites. The Think Tank uses them for clean-up duties and experiments.

Marked Men are mutated survivors of NCR and Legion forces trapped in the Divide, scarred by radiation and storms. They wear patched armor and carry weapons forged from Divide metal, including helmets inspired by Legate Lanius. Rumors of them spread across the West Coast wasteland.

Mongrels are aggressive canine creatures found in the Mojave Wasteland and surrounding regions. Caesar's Legion keeps Mongrels tended by their Houndmasters, with the current mother of the Fort's pack being a female named Lupa. According to Antony, some of these Mongrels fight in the area and generally do not welcome visitors. White Legs Mongrels are also found throughout Zion Canyon, accompanying members of the White Legs tribe.

Nightstalkers are genetic hybrids of coyote and rattlesnake DNA created by Dr. Borous at Big MT before the Great War. They escaped into the Mojave Wasteland and beyond after the bombs fell, hunting in nocturnal packs and nesting in caves. Their bodies combine fur and scales, with dog-like forms, rattlesnake heads and tails, and mismatched eyes.

Ravens are small birds found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, commonly gathering near dead or crucified bodies at sites like Nipton and other Legion-raided locations. They tend to be more prevalent around civilized areas and settlements, becoming scarcer the further one travels from towns. Ravens are harmless creatures that will fly away if approached too closely and will never attack even if harmed. They are often seen in pairs along highways and may gather in places such as Goodsprings Cemetery, the Boulder City Ruins, and near the entrance to Primm.

The PDQ-88b Securitron, also known as the RobCo security model 2060-B, is a security robot created by RobCo Industries and the H&H Tools Factory and charged with protecting the New Vegas Strip. A standard unit is armed with a Gatling laser and a 9mm submachine gun, while the upgraded Mk II operating system enables shoulder-mounted missile launchers, a grenade launching system, and an auto-repair capability that raises combat effectiveness by roughly 235%. Securitrons display a face on a monitor screen and can dispense printed material such as obituaries. Several units were acquired by Big MT for reverse engineering, leading Doctor 0 to create the miniature variant Muggy and to develop a Mk VI operating system, though many Big MT units became berserk and hostile.

Spore carriers are reanimated human corpses colonized by the mutated fungus Beauveria mordicana, originally developed for pest control in Vault 22. The fungus became airborne and spread through the Vault, killing inhabitants within ten to twenty days before reanimating their bodies. Survivors of the Vault 22 outbreak fled to Zion Canyon in 2096, where many succumbed to the infection. Spore carriers can also be found in the X-22 Botanical Garden at Big MT, the original source of the fungus, including a unique specimen known as Patient Zero.

Tunnelers are subterranean predators that emerged when nuclear explosions created The Divide, allowing them to hunt prey on the surface. They reproduce quickly, hunt in large groups, are capable of killing other predators such as Deathclaws, and may even pose a threat to the Mojave Wasteland in the future. The bite of Venomous Tunnelers can be just as lethal as a sting from a Bark Scorpion. As for their origin, Ulysses suspects that they have been around for a long time, and that Radiation might have had an effect on them.

The Alaskan Reclamation Operation was a pre-War military campaign launched by the United States Armed Forces in response to the Chinese invasion of Alaska in 2066. Commanded by General Constantine Chase, the operation saw American forces deploy airships, T-45 power armor units, and deathclaws against Chinese troops. The campaign lasted until January 2077, concluding with the Battle of Anchorage and the full liberation of Alaska. The operation is remembered as one of the most significant conflicts of the Sino-American War.

The Automation Riots were a series of conflicts across the pre-War United States sparked by massive unemployment as advanced robotic systems replaced human workers during the Resource Wars. Labor-intensive jobs in mining and factory work were hit hardest, with cities like Watoga becoming fully automated and workers facing homelessness as early as 2061. The unrest peaked in October 2077 when disenfranchised miners and workers organized roadblocks and strikes across Appalachia, only to face lethal force from Hornwright-funded Strikebreaker robots and National Guard units deploying HalluciGen riot gas. The riots spread from Welch to Beckley, Charleston, Mount Blair, Pittsburgh, and Los Angeles, with miners even seizing the Rockhound excavator on Mount Blair for eight days before combat robots eliminated them.

The Battle of Anchorage, also known as the Liberation of Anchorage, the Anchorage Campaign, and the Anchorage Reclamation, was a major military conflict of the Resource Wars fought between the United States and China. It began when Chinese forces invaded Alaska in the winter of 2066, threatening the Alaskan Pipeline. Under the leadership of General Constantine Chase, the U.S. Army deployed the newly introduced T-51 series power armor and ultimately liberated Anchorage after ten years of fighting.

A Brotherhood Civil War refers to internal conflicts within the Brotherhood of Steel, whether between factions within a single chapter or across multiple chapters. In the Capital Wasteland, a schism formed when Elder Lyons redirected his chapter toward helping local citizens, prompting Paladin Henry Casdin to lead a breakaway faction called the Outcasts away from the Citadel, with hostility between the two groups escalating into violence. A second civil war erupted in 2296 when Elder Cleric Quintus of the Knights of San Fernando sought to use a Cold Fusion Diode to rally other chapters against the Commonwealth Chapter, a conflict further complicated by the arrival of Paladin Xander Harkness and the theft of the diode by Scribe Dane.

The Brotherhood War is a major conflict between the Brotherhood of Steel and the New California Republic, rooted in their disagreement over how technology should be controlled. The conflict spans the former American Southwest and the Mojave Wasteland, with NCR commanders such as Colonel Cassandra Moore having completed multiple tours against the Brotherhood. In 2275, fighting broke out in the Mojave between the NCR and the local Brotherhood chapter, extending to attacks on several Brotherhood bunkers across the region. The following year, the NCR launched Operation Sunburst, attacking and occupying the Brotherhood's fortifications at HELIOS One, where Elder Elijah had refused to retreat despite the location being indefensible.

The Exodus was the post-War journey in which Captain Roger Maxson led the surviving United States Army soldiers and their families away from Mariposa Military Base on October 27, 2077, toward the Lost Hills bunker. The caravan was repeatedly attacked by marauders throughout the trek, and while the soldiers' Power Armor protected them, the unprotected civilians and families suffered high casualties, including Maxson's own wife. A group of soldiers broke off and headed south, never to be heard from again, while a separatist faction led by D. Allen split from the main body against Maxson's wishes and set out for the Glow in hopes of recovering technology stored there.

The food riots were incidents of civil unrest and protests that swept across the United States in response to dwindling food supplies and government rationing. The White House dismissed the protesters, with officials claiming the president himself was suffering by substituting cube steak for prime rib and drinking what they called the detestable Chateau Montrose 2043 wine. In Roxbury, Boston, tensions turned deadly when a hungry crowd stormed a food bank and the soldiers guarding it opened fire on the unarmed civilians, killing four and injuring eight. Witnesses reported that the soldiers appeared to be picking out targets in advance and laughing as they did so.

The Formation of the Brotherhood of Steel occurred at Lost Hills when Roger Maxson officially established the organization over radio contact with Elizabeth Taggerdy of Taggerdy's Thunder in Appalachia. Maxson promised to build something new to reclaim what was lost, modeling the group's mission of preserving knowledge after the knights and scribes following the fall of Rome. Taggerdy and her soldiers were confused by the Brotherhood of Steel name but adopted it anyway. The event is remembered as the founding moment of one of the post-War era's most recognized organizations.

The Glow Expedition was a post-War event in which a faction of Brotherhood of Steel defectors led by Allen attempted to explore the West Tek research facility, also known as the Glow. Allen's group, including Soto, Jensen, and Camarillo, had split from the main Exodus from Mariposa Military Base to Lost Hills, taking weapons and technology with them. After twenty days of travel, they reached the irradiated crater and descended into the facility, believing their power armor and Rad-X supplies would protect them. They explored the first two levels without incident, but functioning security sensors on the third level triggered automated defenses that killed most of the party.

topic: great_war,World War III,War of the Century
topic_desc_basic: The Great War was a global nuclear exchange that occurred on Saturday, October 23, 2077, ending the decade-long Sino-American War between the United States and China. Nuclear missiles were detected that morning, and within hours cities across North America were struck, with the entire exchange lasting roughly two hours and resulting in the deaths of 7.54 billion people. A relative few survived by reaching underground vaults constructed by the Vault-Tec Corporation, while emergency response efforts collapsed due to electromagnetic pulses disabling communications and widespread desertion amid radiation sickness. Hubologists sometimes refer to the event as the Great Deluge, and it has also been called World War III and the War of the Century.

The Invasion of Alaska was a major military conflict that took place as part of the Resource Wars, beginning in the winter of 2066 when China launched a massive assault on American soil in pursuit of Alaska's oil reserves and control of the Alaskan Pipeline. The attack caught American forces off guard despite early warnings, with the scale of the Chinese landing being described as unprecedented. Chinese forces quickly executed a two-pronged assault, targeting both the city of Anchorage and the strategically important Artillery Overlook positioned above it. American soldiers under Captain Zachary Lloyd held the overlook for several hours under heavy bombardment while civilian contractors evacuated, though Anchorage ultimately fell to the Chinese.

The Mariposa Mutiny was an armed uprising in October 2077 at the Mariposa Military Base, led by Captain Roger Maxson and the base security detail after they discovered the nature of the Forced Evolutionary Virus experiments being conducted on human subjects. Colonel Robert Spindel, the nominal commander, suffered a nervous breakdown and committed suicide on October 15, leaving Maxson in permanent command. Maxson interrogated and murdered the research scientists, including chief researcher Robert Anderson and Erin Shellman, who held out the longest. On October 20, 2077, Maxson declared his unit in full secession from the United States, but no government response came, though news of the mutiny spread through the wider United States Army.

The Navarro Conflict was a post-War military engagement between the Enclave and the New California Republic. After the destruction of Control Station ENCLAVE, the Enclave's command structure dissolved, allowing the NCR to take over Navarro, killing everyone who could not escape. The NCR justified the act by stating the Enclave was a threat to the region. Survivors who fled attempted to integrate into the NCR, while an Enclave contingent at Raven Rock remained unaware of the fall of Navarro.

The Resource Wars were a series of global conflicts triggered by an unsustainable economy dependent on finite resources such as petroleum and uranium. Major engagements included the Chinese invasion of Anchorage, Alaska, the annexation of Canada by the United States, and fighting between European powers in the Middle East. The Sino-American War, spanning from 2066 to 2077, saw the United States deploy T-51 Power Armor to the Chinese mainland after reclaiming Anchorage, only for the front to settle into a stalemate with no clear victor. These conflicts were ultimately rendered moot by the Great War on October 23, 2077, when a nuclear exchange between the United States and China killed billions and ended the decade-long struggle.

The Schism was a conflict within the Brotherhood of Steel chapter stationed in the Capital Wasteland, arising from Elder Owyn Lyons' decision to redirect the chapter's efforts toward aiding the region's inhabitants rather than pursuing the Brotherhood's traditional mission of technology recovery. A faction of members who viewed this as a betrayal of their core purpose broke away under the leadership of Paladin Henry Casdin, abandoning the Citadel and adopting the name Brotherhood Outcasts. Tensions between the two groups steadily escalated into open violence, with the Outcasts operating independently and regarding Lyons' loyalists as wayward traitors to the Brotherhood's original charter. The division persisted as a defining feature of the Capital Wasteland's Brotherhood chapter, with both sides maintaining hostile relations toward one another.

The Sino-American War was a major conflict between the United States and China that lasted from 2066 to 2077, driven by the depletion of global oil reserves. It began when Chinese forces under General Jingwei invaded Alaska to secure the last remaining oil supplies, prompting the United States to launch the Alaskan Reclamation Operation led by General Constantine Chase. During the war, the United States annexed Canada to secure a route to Alaska and commissioned the Pan-Immunity Virion Project, which later became the Forced Evolutionary Virus, to counter biological weapons. The conflict ultimately culminated in the Great War on October 23, 2077, when nuclear missiles were launched, rendering the preceding battles moot.

The United States Annexation of Canada, sometimes referred to as the creation of "Little America," occurred prior to the Great War due to the United States' desperate need for Canadian natural resources during the Resource Wars. Tensions began after the Chinese invasion of Anchorage in 2066, when Canadian officials opposed American troops moving through their territory. An attempt to sabotage the Alaskan pipeline finally prompted the U.S. military to announce a complete takeover of all Canadian assets and resources on June 3, 2072.

The Unity Conflict is a post-War event mentioned in Fallout. It is referenced as part of the broader historical background of the wasteland. Little detail is provided beyond its classification as a significant conflict that occurred after the Great War. The Unity Conflict appears in Fallout.

The Battle of Arizona Spillway was a military engagement between Caesar's Legion and the New California Republic, fought at the Arizona Spillway following the Battle of Willow Beach. It formed part of a broader Legion campaign to drive NCR forces from the eastern bank of the Colorado River. The battle resulted in a victory for Caesar's Legion, further weakening the NCR's hold on the region's eastern approaches and contributing to the ongoing tension along the river frontier.

The Battle of Nelson was a military conflict in the Mojave Wasteland in which Caesar's Legion seized the town of Nelson from the New California Republic. General Lee Oliver had occupied Nelson to secure a vulnerable stretch of the Colorado River between Camp Forlorn Hope and Camp Searchlight, but the base had barely enough time to establish proper defenses before the attack. Caesar and Vulpes Inculta, likely acting on intelligence from a mole at Camp McCarran, ordered Decanus Dead Sea to lead two contubernia against the under-equipped NCR troopers. Despite being outnumbered two to one, the legionaries swiftly overran the defenses, killed most of the troopers, and hurled the rest into the Colorado River in full view of spotters from Camp Forlorn Hope.

The Battle of Willow Beach was a military conflict between Caesar's Legion and the New California Republic that occurred at Camp Willow following the First Battle of Hoover Dam. This engagement marked the return to open hostilities between the two factions and was the first Legion strike since the initial battle at the dam. Legion forces led the assault in a bid to push the NCR out of the eastern side of the Colorado River, resulting in the destruction of the NCR camp. Along with the subsequent Battle of Arizona Spillway, this clash forced the NCR back across the river and gave the Legion complete control of its eastern side.

The Bitter Springs Massacre occurred in the Mojave Wasteland around 2278, when New California Republic forces attacked a Great Khan encampment they believed to be a raider hideout. The Great Khans had previously harassed and raided NCR settlers, soldiers, and civilians, prompting the operation. NCR First Recon sharpshooters were positioned to cover the canyon's only escape route, but when the main assault was spotted early, fleeing Khan non-combatants including women, children, and the elderly poured into the pass. The sharpshooters radioed for confirmation of their shoot-on-sight orders, but the commanding major froze and a subordinate confirmed the order, leading to the slaughter of the fleeing civilians.

The First Battle of Hoover Dam was Caesar's Legion's assault on New California Republic forces at Hoover Dam in 2277, led on the Legion side by the Malpais Legate, also known as Joshua Graham. NCR forces under Chief Hanlon, including First Recon and NCR Rangers, executed a tactical retreat into Boulder City, where they had laid explosives throughout the town. When the Legion's elite forces pursued them inside, the explosives were detonated, inflicting severe casualties and crippling the offensive, after which General Lee Oliver's troops counter-attacked and routed the Legion's main force. Caesar punished his failed legate by setting Joshua Graham on fire and casting him into the Grand Canyon, while a memorial at Boulder City honors the over one hundred NCR soldiers who lost their lives in the battle.

The Mojave Campaign is a New California Republic military operation launched in 2274 when President Aaron Kimball sent forces to occupy Hoover Dam after scouts discovered it intact the previous year. Upon arrival, NCR troops encountered Mr. House's forces, and negotiations led to a treaty allowing the NCR to occupy the dam and establish a base at McCarran Airport, with 95% of the dam's electricity sent to NCR home states and the remainder to the Strip. The NCR also established an embassy on the Strip.

The NCR-Legion War is an ongoing military conflict between the New California Republic and Caesar's Legion over control of the Mojave Wasteland. Tensions rose after the NCR occupied Hoover Dam in 2274, leading to the First Battle of Hoover Dam in 2277, where NCR sharpshooters and rigged explosives in Boulder City repelled the Legion's forces. The conflict has seen significant casualties on both sides, with the Legion employing brutal tactics such as irradiating Camp Searchlight and destroying the settlements of Hopeville and Ashton. The war remains unresolved as both factions vie for dominance in the region.

The NCRCF Prison Break was a convict revolt at the NCR Correctional Facility, a former pre-War Jean Conservancy site repurposed by the NCR to house prisoners used for railroad labor. When most NCR guards were reassigned to the Colorado River, anti-NCR revolutionary Samuel Cooke organized inmates to stockpile blasting powder and makeshift weapons, then blasted their way out, killing the warden and nearly all remaining guards. Afterward the convicts fragmented into several groups, including the Powder Gangers under Eddie who stayed to raid the surrounding areas, Cooke's followers who departed for Vault 19, and a smaller group that took over the Bison Steve Hotel in Primm. The uprising disrupted the region severely, allowing deathclaws to nest at Quarry Junction and effectively shutting down I-15 to New Vegas.

Operation: Sunburst was a major conflict in 2276 between the Brotherhood of Steel and the New California Republic at HELIOS One. Father Elijah led the Mojave chapter there after becoming distracted by the ARCHIMEDES II solar weapon. The NCR outnumbered the Brotherhood and assaulted the facility from all sides. Despite superior equipment, the Brotherhood suffered heavy losses and was forced to retreat to Hidden Valley under Paladin McNamara's command.

The Sierra Madre Gala Event was a planned celebration at the Sierra Madre Casino, intended to gather celebrities and high society figures. It was scheduled for the night of October 23, 2077, the same night the Great War devastated the world. The event was meant to feature lights in the sky, music filling the villa streets, and a grand finale of fireworks that would open the casino's gates, offering attendees a chance to begin again. The event never occurred as planned due to the nuclear war.

The Ultra-Luxe Shootout was a gun battle that occurred on July 13, 2072, at the Ultra-Luxe Casino on the Las Vegas Strip, between a group of men labeled as mobsters and the Las Vegas police force. According to the Charleston Herald, police stormed the casino floor and exchanged fire with the group, resulting in the deaths of all five individuals and injuries to seventeen bystanders. Eyewitness accounts conflicted, with some claiming soldiers arrived with a missile launcher while others said the violence began with sniper fire, and witnesses reported the group attempted to surrender on two occasions. The Las Vegas chief of police declared the incident a major victory, stating that no one in Las Vegas was above the law.

The West Side Massacre was a violent confrontation in New Reno in which the Salvatore family attacked members of the Bishop and Mordino crime families. Two of Salvatore's enforcers eliminated a group of rival thugs who had been encroaching on Salvatore territory in the West Side district. The Salvatores' use of laser pistols gave them a decisive advantage over their opponents, allowing them to kill the rival gang members with relative ease. The massacre resulted in an uneasy peace among the families, while the Mordinos quietly planned their revenge against the Salvatores.

The Brotherhood of Steel, often abbreviated as BoS or BOS, is a paramilitary organization founded by Captain Roger Maxson after he deserted the United States Army just before the Great War. The various chapters across the post-War United States share a core mission of seizing and regulating pre-War technology to prevent its abuse and ensure the survival of humanity. Their ranks include paladins, knights, and scribes, and they operate under the motto Ad Victoriam. Notable chapters include the founding group at Lost Hills, an expeditionary force in the Capital Wasteland led by Elder Lyons, and a Mojave contingent that recently suffered significant losses to the New California Republic at HELIOS One.

The Enclave is a remnant of America's pre-War government, originally formed as a secret contingent within the United States continuity of government system and described by some as a militarized shadow government. Comprised of presidents, military leaders, industrialists, and scientists, the Enclave made contingency plans before the Great War, securing installations such as the presidential oil rig, Raven Rock, and the congressional bunker. After the nuclear exchange, the organization became a fascist paramilitary group with totalitarian goals, making multiple attempts to reassert control over the wasteland through the use of the Forced Evolutionary Virus to eliminate all mutated life, which they viewed as cleansing the world. Their genocidal agenda brought them into conflict with groups such as the New California Republic and the Brotherhood of Steel, resulting in the destruction of many Enclave outposts including the oil rig and Camp Navarro, though remnants continue to operate in scattered regions.

The Apostles of the Eternal Light are a religious faction based in the ruins of Springvale and led by Mother Curie III, a former devotee of the Children of Atom. Unlike the Children of Atom, the Apostles actively irradiate themselves and only those who have been baptized in Atom's holy Light are permitted into their Holy Light Monastery, whose surface entrance is guarded by Brother Gerard. The Apostles regard ghouls as enlightened beings who have given themselves to the Eternal Light. They also differ from the Children of Atom in Megaton by opposing the Great Division and the idea of detonating the Megaton bomb.

The Brotherhood Outcasts, often simply called the Outcasts, are a renegade faction that split from the Capital Wasteland's Brotherhood of Steel under the leadership of Paladin Henry Casdin. They oppose Elder Lyons' policies, believing they are the true loyalists upholding the Brotherhood's original mission of discovering and securing advanced pre-War technology. After departing the Citadel with a significant portion of its stockpiles, they seized Fort Independence as their headquarters, painting their power armor red and black to distinguish themselves. The group patrols the wasteland for technology and hopes to eventually regroup with the Western Brotherhood chapters to vindicate their actions.

topic: children_of_atom,Church of the Children of Atom
topic_desc_basic: The Children of Atom, sometimes called the Church of the Children of Atom, are a religious cult devoted to the worship of Atom, a deity they associate with nuclear power and radiation. They operate out of Megaton, a settlement built around an undetonated atomic bomb, and helped construct the town in exchange for the bomb remaining in place. The group is led by Confessor Cromwell and Mother Maya, both of whom still reside in Megaton. Members believe the Great War was a holy event perpetrated by Atom, that those who died in it were fortunate to aid in his creation, and that irradiated water is a blessing full of Atom's Light.

The Chinese Remnants are the surviving remnants of Chinese military operations in the United States, consisting of former spies, intelligence agents, and special-ops soldiers who were transformed into ghouls following the Great War. These ghoulified Chinese personnel continue to operate in the Capital Wasteland, with known presences at Mama Dolce's and in underground sewers near Broadcast Tower KT8. The group maintains a military structure, with sergeants and officers demonstrating greater combat proficiency than their subordinates. They are hostile to outsiders encountered in the wasteland.

Littlehorn & Associates is a contract killing firm operating in the Capital Wasteland, headed by Daniel Littlehorn from a large shed at the entrance to the scrapyard. The organization serves as a counterpart to the Regulators and maintains a low-key presence throughout the region, with employees spread across the wasteland. Daniel Littlehorn claims to seek ears from good people as a way of maintaining a certain balance in the wastes, though the firm keeps personal and business information to a minimum to ensure smooth operations. The firm's members include Daniel Littlehorn and his secretaries, who display a remarkably callous attitude toward one another's deaths.

Lyons' Pride, commonly known as the Pride, is an elite tactical unit of Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel formed by Elder Owyn Lyons to combat the super mutant presence in Washington, D.C. The squad is commanded by Sentinel Sarah Lyons, who personally selects its members from a pool of applicants. Operating primarily out of the Galaxy News Radio outpost in Chevy Chase and the Lyons' Den within the Citadel, the group is easily recognized by their T-45d power armor bearing a unique lion rampant insignia. In 2277, the Pride suffered casualties when Initiates Reddin and Jennings were killed during a mission to reinforce the radio outpost against super mutant attacks.

The Nuka-Cola fan club is an association of Nuka-Cola enthusiasts based in the Capital Wasteland, founded by Sierra Petrovita, who serves as its president, recording secretary, and treasurer. Ronald Laren is the only other member, though membership is open to the public. Club activities include collecting Nuka-Cola related items, hosting an annual cook-off featuring recipes containing Nuka-Cola, and awarding the best collection with the Nuka-Cola Fan Club Collection Award. Sierra has won the collection award for ten consecutive years and also won the most recent cook-off with her poached roach with Nuka-sauce.

The Pitt Raiders, also known as Ashur's army, are a group of slavers who rule over the Pitt Slaves in The Pitt following the Scourge. They were united by Ishmael Ashur, a former Brotherhood of Steel member who was left behind during the Brotherhood's purge of the area and later discovered the potential of an operational steel mill. To maintain their workforce, the Pitt Raiders engage in slavery and purchase slaves from the Capital Wasteland, acting as customers of the Paradise Falls Slavers.

The Pitt Slaves are the captive workforce of The Pitt, forced to labor under the constant watch of the Pitt Raiders to keep the city's steel industry running. They suffer from the Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion, a disease that renders all of the Pitt's inhabitants infertile and gradually transforms some into Wildmen or Trogs. Despite their grim circumstances, the slaves harbor hopes of revolution, organized under the leadership of Wernher and Midea, who seek to obtain a cure held by Lord Ashur. Most slaves are found in Downtown and The Mill, with some sent into the hazardous Steelyard to collect steel ingots.

The Point Lookout tribals are a group inhabiting the Ark & Dove Cathedral in the Point Lookout swamplands. They cultivate Punga plants and meditate, led by a man named Jackson, who believes the psychic entity Calvert is a god and follows his commands. New members are initiated by traveling to the Sacred Bog to retrieve Punga Seeds from the Mother Punga, a process that exposes them to hallucinogenic gas and involves the removal of part of their brain to free their mind. The procedure sometimes kills prospective members or strips away more brain functions than intended, leaving those unable to care for themselves under the supervision of a tribal named Woodrose.

The Regulators are a faction in the Capital Wasteland dedicated to bringing evildoers to justice. They appeared within the last ten years and are led by Sonora Cruz, operating out of their headquarters. Megaton sheriff Lucas Simms is counted among their members. The Regulators pursue those with evil reputations and offer bounties for proof of wrongdoers' deaths.

Reilly's Rangers is a mercenary faction operating in the Capital Wasteland, based at the Ranger Compound near Seward Square. The group was founded by Reilly when she was twenty-six years old and has built a reputation as guns for hire who operate under a code of ethics and strive to help people. This moral stance has put them at odds with fellow mercenary group Talon Company, whom they view as lacking any such code. The Rangers have taken on contracts to map Washington, D.C.

The slavers are a faction operating out of Paradise Falls in the Capital Wasteland, with a long history of capturing wastelanders for profit. Under past leaders like Harmon Jurley and Penelope Chase, they overran settlements such as Rockopolis and sold its citizens to the Pitt. Currently led by Eulogy Jones, the slavers are paid on commission and traffic their captives either to local buyers or wealthier regions outside the Capital Wasteland. Small teams roam the wilderness hunting for slaves, while a growing abolitionist movement has begun to threaten their trade.

Sudden-Death Overtime is a mercenary gang operating in the Capital Wasteland around 2277. The group is led by Goalie Ledoux and includes members Centre Dubois, Winger Gervais, and Winger Mercier. They are obsessed with the pre-War sport of ice hockey, though their understanding of it is deeply flawed, as they refer to themselves as an ice gang and believe the primary purpose of the sport was fighting rather than scoring goals. Ledoux and his crew use hockey terminology in their speech, referencing face-offs and crossing sticks.

Talon Company is the largest mercenary organization active in the Capital Wasteland, with operatives found throughout the region. They are hostile to most groups on sight and prioritize cash and loot above all else, hiring themselves out to anyone willing to pay. The group works for an unknown benefactor charged with keeping the Capital Wasteland a lawless place, and their ruthlessness is well documented-Reilly of Reilly's Rangers reports that they killed an entire settlement a year or two ago. Their headquarters displays a flag depicting a large bird with a skull carrying away a crying baby, and they maintain artillery support teams deployed in Seward Square and Takoma Park.

Tenpenny Tower Security is a group of mercenaries hired by Mister Burke to protect Tenpenny Tower, the upscale residential high-rise in the Capital Wasteland. They serve as the tower's armed enforcement, screening visitors and maintaining order within the settlement's walls. The security personnel are generally regarded as little more than hired guns, distinguished by their uniforms and the authority granted to them by the tower's leadership. Their presence ensures that the wealthy residents of Tenpenny Tower remain insulated from the dangers of the wasteland outside.

The Family is a group of nocturnal cannibals who identify as vampires and dwell in Meresti Metro Station east of Arefu. Vance leads them, teaching members to restrain their hunger for human flesh and consume only blood, framing their cannibalism as a wasteland survival adaptation. Prospective members meditate in solitude before joining and must follow the group's rules. The Family repeatedly raids Arefu and recently captured Ian West, an Arefu resident overwhelmed by cannibalism after killing his parents.

The Treeminders are a peaceful religious cult that inhabits and protects Oasis, a verdant vale in the northern Capital Wasteland, where they worship a being they call the Great One, the One Who Grows, the One Who Gives, and the One Who Guides. The Great One is in fact Harold, an FEV mutant who took root in the late 2250s after a tree grew from his head and consumed his body, and whose presence transformed the barren hillside into a lush haven of plant and animal life. The group was founded by a wanderer who took the name Tree Father Birch after he discovered Harold and resolved to protect him from exploitation by others who might seek to do him harm. The Treeminders follow a loose hierarchy led by the Tree Father and Leaf Mother, with branchtenders serving as guardians, bloomseers as healers and interpreters of premonitions, and saplings as the youngest members still learning the ways of Oasis.

Vault 101 Security is the law enforcement division of Vault 101, operating from a centralized office on the upper level. They are the only inhabitants permitted to carry 10mm Pistols and police batons, wearing helmets, armor, utility jumpsuits, and Pip-Boy 3000s. Officers like Kendall are known to patrol the vault and respond to disturbances such as radroach infestations.

The Alpha Team, also known as the 1st Recon Alpha Team, is a division of the New California Republic Army stationed at Camp McCarran. For six months, they have been fighting against the Fiends who have committed acts of violence in the surrounding area. The team is led by Gorobets and includes members such as 10 of Spades, Betsy, Corporal Sterling, and Sergeant Bitter-Root.

The Boomers are an isolationist tribe living at Nellis Air Force Base, descended from Vault 34 dwellers who rebelled against their overseer and escaped with the vault's armory. They earned their nickname from outsiders due to their reverence for explosives, which forms the foundation of their culture and ideology. Led by Mother Pearl and a council of elders including Master-At-Arms Raquel, the Boomers maintain a self-sufficient community with schools, a museum, greenhouses, and solar power. They are deeply paranoid and hostile to outsiders, using artillery and spotters to guard their perimeter, and forbid their own members from leaving Nellis.

The Bright Brotherhood is a religious cult of ghouls based in the REPCONN Test Site west of Novac. Led by the prophetic Glowing One Jason Bright, the group worships a figure known as The Creator and seeks to escape the bigotry of humans by embarking on a "Great Journey" to a promised land using repaired REPCONN rockets. Their ranks also include a single human named Chris Haversam, who fully believes himself to be a ghoul. The Brotherhood is currently hindered by a nightkin invasion in their facility, as the super mutants are convinced the ghouls are hoarding a shipment of Stealth Boys.

Caesar's Legion is a large slaving empire founded in 2247 by Edward Sallow, also known as Caesar, and Joshua Graham, the Malpais Legate. Modeled after ancient Rome, the Legion erases tribal identities to forge a unified warrior culture that controls Arizona, New Mexico, and parts of Utah and Colorado. By 2281, the Legion has expanded into the Mojave Wasteland, establishing a base at Fortification Hill and clashing with the New California Republic over Hoover Dam. The Legion forbids chems and alcohol, treats women as breeding stock, and punishes homosexuality with death, while its citizens believe Caesar rules by divine right as the son of Mars.

Cassidy Caravans is a small caravan company founded and owned by Rose of Sharon Cassidy, commonly known as Cass, in the Mojave Wasteland. Despite its modest size, the company became a notable competitor to larger outfits like the Crimson Caravan by securing consistent trade with core customers such as the New California Republic. Cass established the business after realizing her nomadic wanderings between settlements could be turned profitable, eventually hiring additional staff to handle deliveries along her routes. The company persisted through the brutal caravan conflicts that plagued the Mojave, but in 2281 a covert attack staged by the Van Graffs in collusion with Crimson Caravan manager Alice McLafferty destroyed the caravan and its cargo, leaving Cassidy Caravans with little to its name and Cass stranded at the Mojave Outpost trying to clear her papers.

The Chairmen are one of the Three Families that operate casinos on the New Vegas Strip under the employ of Mr. House. Originally a nomadic warrior tribe called the Mojave Boot-Riders, they accepted House's offer to come to Vegas after their leader Bingo was killed in a duel by Benny, who supported the arrangement. Upon arriving, the tribe was given control of The Tops casino and renamed the Chairmen.

The Dead Horses are a tribe living in Zion Canyon, descended from refugees from Res, east of the Grand Canyon. They speak a language combining their own with that of travelers present during the Great War. They reside at Dead Horse Point and consider pre-War areas taboo, marked with white hand prints. The tribe hunts bighorners for food, commemorating hunts and special occasions with tattoos, while being mindful of the environment.

The Enclave Remnants are scattered veterans of the West Coast Enclave living in the Mojave Wasteland. After the destruction of the Poseidon Energy Oil Rig, some Enclave members retreated to Camp Navarro, but a New California Republic offensive forced them to flee and attempt to integrate into society while avoiding bounty hunters, NCR forces, and the Brotherhood of Steel. The surviving members eventually settled in and around the Mojave, stashing their old equipment in a hidden bunker that once served as a refueling station. Their former commanding officer, Judah Kreger, maintained the group's connection over the years, though he no longer issues orders.

The Fiends are a raider gang composed entirely of chem addicts operating in the Mojave Wasteland around New Vegas. After killing the inhabitants of Vault 3, they claimed the facility as their base and grew strong enough to control a large part of the southwestern New Vegas conurbation. The group is led by Motor-Runner, Violet, Cook-Cook, and Driver Nephi, and they attack anyone on sight except the Great Khans, who supply them with chems. The NCR seeks to eliminate the Fiends but is limited to holding defensive lines, while Caesar's Legion views their drug dependence with contempt and the Omertas consider them bad for business due to their theft of weapon shipments and kidnapping of locals.

The Followers of the Apocalypse, often called simply the Followers, are a humanitarian organization founded by former vault dwellers and others who originally lived near the Glow in San Diego. Led by Nicole, who lost her parents during the group's migration north, the Followers were established on the principle of ending cycles of violence by sharing knowledge and resources freely. They are not a religious group but are guided by a set of ideals centered on education, medicine, and research, with the aim of rebuilding civilization to its pre-War state. By 2280, the Followers maintained outposts in every major city within the New California Republic, with their headquarters at the Boneyard Library, and a regional hub at the Old Mormon Fort in the Mojave Wasteland under administrator Julie Farkas.

The Great Khans are a raider tribe based in Red Rock Canyon in the Mojave Wasteland. Descended from the New Khans of California, the tribe migrated east under Papa Khan and clashed with the New California Republic, culminating in the Bitter Springs Massacre. The surviving Khans resettled in Red Rock Canyon, where they sustain themselves through chem production and trafficking, trading with nearby Fiends and Westside residents. Papa Khan seeks an alliance with Caesar's Legion to oppose the NCR and restore the tribe's glory, though the Legion intends to absorb the Khans after using them.

The Kings are a gang operating in Freeside, the area outside the New Vegas Strip gates, sometimes called the Kings of Freeside by NCR citizens. They follow The King, the most powerful individual in Freeside, and copy the mannerisms and looks of the individual the King's School of Impersonation was founded to emulate. The gang works alongside the Followers of the Apocalypse to keep Freeside peaceful and independent, defending the area against squatters and thugs while running the water pump installed by Bill Ronte of the Followers. The Kings believe that every man is free to follow his own path and that no one has the right to trample on the freedoms of others, though tensions have risen as New California Republic citizens move into the area, causing conflict with locals.

The Mojave Express is a delivery company that emerged alongside the NCR's eastward expansion, carrying letters and packages across the vast distances of the American Southwest. It maintains offices in The Hub, where couriers are hired, and in Primm within the Mojave Wasteland. The company operates dropboxes at several locations throughout the Mojave, including Goodsprings, Novac, Freeside, and the New Vegas Strip, allowing for the transfer of items between distant points. By 2280, the Mojave Express had not yet extended its reach as far as New Reno.

The New California Republic, often abbreviated as the NCR, is a large democratic nation spanning portions of the American southwest. Founded by Vault dwellers who established the settlement of Shady Sands, the republic grew to encompass five states and a population of over 700,000 citizens. Dedicated to the rule of law, the nation outlaws practices like slavery and maintains a standing army, currency, and court system. Under the leadership of President Aaron Kimball, the NCR continues to expand its influence into the Mojave Wasteland, though some tribes know them as the Sunset People.

The Omertas are one of the Three Families of the New Vegas Strip, running the Gomorrah casino under the leadership of Nero and his right-hand man Big Sal, with underboss Cachino handling lesser tasks. Before Mr. House recruited them, they were the Slither Kin, a nomadic tribe that lured travelers into camp, drugged them, and murdered or enslaved them. The Omertas run scams, extortion, and prostitution from Gomorrah, keeping workers dependent through chem addiction and ruthlessly pursuing unpaid debts.

The Powder Gangers, sometimes called Powder Gangsters, are a gang of escaped prisoners operating in the Mojave Wasteland. They originated from a prison break at the NCR Correctional Facility, where inmates were previously forced to maintain a railroad under military supervision. Led by Samuel Cooke, the prisoners overwhelmed the guards and dispersed into various groups, with some taking over the facility under Eddie and others joining Cooke in Vault 19. Known for their heavy use of dynamite, they have disrupted local infrastructure by shutting down Highway 93 and Quarry Junction.

The Sorrows are a peaceful tribe living in Zion Canyon, known for their hunting and fishing-based culture rather than a warrior tradition. Their signature weapon is the Yao Guai Gauntlet, crafted during a rite of passage where young members hunt and kill a Yao Guai. The Sorrows worship a spirit known as the Father in the Cave, who provided gifts and guidance to the original Sorrows, a group of children who escaped a place called The School. Their shaman White Bird oversees religious rites, and the tribe believes that when they die, the river carries their water to the next life to be with the Father.

The State of Utobitha is a faction of Super Mutants and Nightkin occupying Black Mountain in the Mojave Wasteland, founded and ruled by the Nightkin Tabitha, who styles herself supreme commander. Black Mountain was originally settled peacefully by first generation Super Mutants led by Marcus, but an influx of Nightkin and second generation Super Mutants drove Marcus and his followers away to found Jacobstown, leaving Tabitha in control. Tabitha broadcasts propaganda and orders to kill humans on sight over Black Mountain Radio, describing Utobitha as a utopian society for mutants, though Nightkin receive preferential treatment. The inhabitants are hostile to outsiders, wary of the NCR and Caesar's Legion, and maintain their weapons and scrap-built shelters, though they struggle to keep the communications outpost running without outside mechanical help.

The Misfits are a small squad of New California Republic Army troopers assigned to 9th Platoon at Camp Golf in 2281. Their commanding officer, Sergeant McCredie, is frustrated by their poor discipline, work ethic, and camaraderie, though he retains some faith in the squad's informal leader, Mags. Each member of the Misfits serves with ulterior motives or under duress rather than genuine dedication. Mags originally sought to become an NCR Ranger but was unable to do so and settled for the regular army.

The Van Graffs are a prominent merchant house and crime family operating out of Redding, dealing primarily in energy weapons and high-value commodities. Founded by a ruthless matriarch who relies on her ten children to manage her mercantile empire, the family has a long history of clashing with the New California Republic. By 2281, they have expanded into the Mojave Wasteland, taking over the Silver Rush casino in Freeside under the management of Gloria Van Graff. To secure a lucrative defense contract with the NCR, Gloria orchestrates a trap against Caesar's Legion while simultaneously forming a covert alliance with the Crimson Caravan to undercut local competitors.

The Vipers are an aggressive tribe of raiders originating from Vault 15, founded by Jonathan Faust after a quasi-religious experience involving a pit of vipers that led to their worship of snakes and the foundation of their religion, The Winding Way of the Great Snake. Their faith involves a caste system of priests and warriors, rites using viper venom to evoke visions, and a deity known as the Great Snake or God of the Pit, to whom Faust claimed regular sacrifices were demanded. Faust led the Vipers for 28 years until his death during a raid on the Brotherhood of Steel, after which both the Brotherhood and the New California Republic hunted the Vipers nearly to extinction, fracturing the survivors into small clans that resorted to opportunistic raiding across the Mojave. By 2280, the remaining Vipers had become known for raiding around the New Reno area and occupying territory east of Vegas, though much of their original culture had been lost, with many acting merely as gunslingers rather than religious fanatics.

The Westside Cooperative, sometimes called the Westside Co-op, is a tight-knit community faction based in the fortified Westside zone of the Mojave Wasteland. Founded by New Reno immigrant Clayton Ettienne and local farmers, the organization pools resources to grow crops for sustenance and sells surplus produce to travelers and larger factions. With the help of engineer Tom Anderson and the Followers of the Apocalypse, the group refurbished an old commercial building to house their farming operation and a grocery store managed by Ettienne. The Cooperative shares its earned caps among the farmers, though it currently faces tense negotiations with the NCR over the siphoning of their water supplies.

The White Glove Society is one of the Three Families responsible for operating the Ultra-Luxe casino on the New Vegas Strip. Originally a cannibalistic tribe, they were employed by Mr. House and agreed to abandon their tribal identity and cannibalism in exchange for him concealing their former name. The society maintains an atmosphere of refinement and mystery, with members wearing formal wear and masks while providing the Strip's most elite casino experience.

The White Legs are a post-war tribal group originally from the ruins of Salt Lake City, known for raiding and scavenging throughout the Great Basin and Colorado Plains. They periodically raided northeast of Caliente until the Desert Rangers were absorbed into the NCR, after which they regularly raided the stretch of I-15, causing travelers to avoid the area. After the Legion's defeat at the First Battle of Hoover Dam, Caesar ordered New Canaan destroyed and the White Legs, intent on joining the Legion, were given a rite of passage to eradicate the city. Ulysses helped teach the White Legs to wage war, leading them to an armory near Spanish Fork where they discovered large submachine guns they call storm drums, which became their signature weapon.

The United States, also known as America or the U.S.A., was a pre-War global superpower and the primary setting of the Fallout series. Before the Great War on October 23, 2077, the nation was governed by a President and Congress, with the United States Armed Forces serving as its unified military. Following the devastating nuclear exchange, the country ceased to exist as a centralized political entity, fracturing into a collection of independent settlements and successor states. Remnants of its government and culture, such as the Enclave, continue to influence post-War society across the former territories.

Adams Air Force Base is a former pre-War military installation located outside the Capital Wasteland, accessible via the Presidential Metro. After the Great War, the Enclave occupied the facility and made use of its Mobile Base Crawler, a large mobile research platform. The base served as a fortified Enclave compound and, following the loss of Raven Rock, became a key fallback position for the organization's remaining forces in the region. The facility housed Enclave soldiers, scientists, Vertibird support infrastructure, and research operations on Wasteland creatures, including caged Deathclaws.

Anacostia Crossing Station is a Metro station and the southernmost stop on the Red Line, situated directly north of Rivet City. The station entrance lies just north of the tower platform that links the Rivet City access bridge to the riverbank. Below, the station is inhabited by lightly armed raiders who have established an encampment behind sandbag barricades on the raised central platform. The tunnels of Anacostia Crossing allow transit to The Mall and Seward Square, and a Super Mutant camp rests just west of the station, overlooking the Jefferson Memorial.

The Anchorage Memorial is a monument located on an island in the Potomac River within the Capital Wasteland, commemorating the Battle of Anchorage in Alaska. After the Great War, wastelanders herded mirelurks into the facility and established a meat processing operation, selling mirelurk meat to passing traders for caps. A competitor hired mercenaries who released the mirelurks, resulting in the creatures killing the facility's inhabitants. The memorial contains multiple structural levels, including living quarters, offices, and underground maintenance areas now infested with mirelurks and their nests.

Arefu is a small settlement in the Capital Wasteland situated on an overpass bridge spanning the Potomac River northwest of Vault 106. It serves as a stopping point on the trading caravan circuit and is the last stop on most trade routes from Megaton. In recent years, the settlement's population has dwindled from thirty down to only five residents. To maintain security, the inhabitants destroyed the northern span of the bridge, leaving only a single entrance to defend against the dangers of the wasteland.

The Bethesda Ruins are the remains of a major pre-War town located northwest of Washington, D.C., formerly served by metro and highway systems. The ruins are divided into Bethesda Offices West, Bethesda Offices East, and the Bethesda Underworks. Prior to the Great War, the city featured a local park named after its largest employer where residents regularly played baseball. By 2277, the area is heavily barricaded and inhabited by hostile Raiders and Feral Ghouls.

Big Town is a makeshift settlement in the Capital Wasteland located north of Vault 101 and southeast of the Moonbeam Outdoor Cinema. It is surrounded by barricades and a makeshift moat, accessible only by a bridge at the north end, with walls built from cars, debris, and rubble. The population consists mostly of teenagers and young adults who were expelled from Little Lamplight upon turning sixteen, having been told that Big Town was a safe and comfortable place for mungos to live. The settlement has been ravaged by Super Mutant and Slaver attacks, and some residents have been kidnapped by Super Mutants and taken to the old police station in Germantown.

Canterbury Commons is a small trading post and town on the eastern edge of the Capital Wasteland, founded by Uncle Roe and his sister Daisy as a trading center for caravan merchants. Raider attacks killed Daisy and her husband Louis, leaving Roe to maintain the settlement with his nephew Derek Pacion. The town is currently caught in a conflict between two self-styled superhumans: Tanya Christoff, known as the AntAgonizer, who seeks to destroy Canterbury Commons believing it a blight on the wasteland, and Scott Wollinski, who adopted the Mechanist persona to defend the town after the AntAgonizer destroyed his favorite robot. The settlement's only permanent merchant is Joe Porter, who operates out of an old Dot's Diner, while Dominic and Machete live in an adjacent garage and Roe resides in the old fire station.

The Capital Wasteland, also called the Capital Region, encompasses the ruins of Washington, D.C. and surrounding areas, stretching from Raven Rock in the northwest to Rivet City in the southeast. During the Great War, the area received advanced warning after the west coast was destroyed, but those unable to secure space in vaults sought shelter in metro tunnels, museums, and other alternate shelters, while insufficiently equipped National Guard aid stations led to desertion and high mortality. By 2277, settlements such as Megaton, Canterbury Commons, Arefu, and the Republic of Dave dotted the landscape, connected by trade caravans, and Elder Lyons' Brotherhood of Steel had established a base at the Citadel to combat the Super Mutant threat and protect scientists working on Project Purity.

Chaste Acres Dairy Farm is the ruin of a small farm in the northeastern Capital Wasteland, situated southwest of the Republic of Dave. The site has been taken over by a group of raiders, who frequently find themselves under attack by roaming creatures such as robots, yao guai, giant radscorpions, or even deathclaws. The farm includes a grain silo with a sniper position above and a barn containing a corpse on the second floor. A Nuka-Cola delivery truck sits straight west of the farm, and a note about it can be found in Old Olney.

The Chryslus Building is a ruined office building on the outskirts of Washington, D.C. in the Capital Wasteland. It was once the headquarters of Chryslus Motors, the pre-War automobile manufacturer, and included a baseball field constructed outside for employee use. Since the Great War, the building has fallen into considerable ruin and become a stronghold occupied by Super Mutants and Centaurs.

Clifftop Shacks are a fortified encampment perched on a cliff southeast of Oasis in the Capital Wasteland. The site consists of a small plateau bearing three shacks, two of which remain accessible, reachable by an uphill path on the eastern side and a suspension bridge on the western side. The encampment is inhabited by Super Mutants, who have festooned the area with gore bags, and at times Centaurs can be found among them. The northern shack holds a collection of ruined books and a skeleton resting on a bloodied bed, while the southern shack contains makeshift bedding along with the remains of a raider and a wastelander.

The Corvega Factory is a pre-War Corvega facility southwest of Vault 108 in the Capital Wasteland that manufactured vehicles used throughout the United States. It is now home to a colony of giant ants, including a giant ant queen at the southern end of the factory. The factory also contains the bodies of mercenaries and raiders who failed to reach the queen, along with a small number of feral ghouls.

The County Sewer Mainline is a tunnel system in the Capital Wasteland that can be entered from the Sewer Waystation or a sewage grate along the Potomac north of a raider camp near the Key Bridge. It runs beneath Grayditch and Arlington National Cemetery but offers no access points at either location. The tunnels are home to a hostile ghoul named Gallo, who keeps a small Nuka-Cola collection and a pen of radroaches in his room past a series of traps. Feral ghouls and radroaches occupy much of the sewer management area, and the remains of dead mercenaries and wastelanders litter the passages throughout.

The Deathclaw Sanctuary is a cave maze in the Capital Wasteland, located between Dickerson Tabernacle Chapel and Broadcast Tower KB5. It is home to numerous Deathclaws and contains piles of maimed bodies and body parts, serving as both a nest and storage place. The interior is dark and maze-like, with twisting tunnels and large obstructions making it one of the most dangerous places in the region. Outside the sanctuary, a small overhang conceals a dead mercenary and a footlocker, while Deathclaws guard the entrance.

The Dunwich Building is an office building located at the southwesternmost edge of the Capital Wasteland, south of Girdershade and far west of Tenpenny Tower. Before the Great War, it was owned by Dunwich Borers LLC, a company that manufactured rock drills for tunneling and drilling operations. After the war, the building remains standing and is known among wastelanders as a place of bad mojo, with reports of strange phenomena such as self-opening doors, unexplained footsteps, flickering lights, and disturbing hallucinations. The interior is divided into three sections: the entrance, the Forsaken Dunwich Ruins, and the Virulent Underchambers, all of which are infested with feral ghouls.
