Galaxy News Radio, often abbreviated as GNR, was a pre-War radio station based in Washington, D.C. and a subsidiary of Galaxy News Network, originally broadcasting on 103.8 FM with programs such as Mornings with Marie. In the Capital Wasteland, the station has been repurposed by Three Dog from the GNR Building Plaza, who reports on happenings around the region with the help of a technician named Margaret. Three Dog operates the station as part of what he calls the "Good Fight," his attempt to inform inhabitants how "things really are" and expose the Enclave's true intentions. The station plays a combination of Three Dog's commentary and twenty songs from records found in playable condition, though its signal quality is poor due to a relay dish on the Washington Monument that was destroyed when a Super Mutant shot it to pieces.

The Greener Pastures Disposal Site is one of the largest radioactive areas in the Capital Wasteland, located northwest of the Temple of the Union, southwest of Old Olney, and northeast of the MDPL-13 Power Station. Before the Great War, Greener Pastures was an infamous radioactive waste-disposal plant that was in reality a dumping ground for all kinds of toxic waste, liberally stored in the open without any containment or deactivation. It became one of the biggest environmental disasters in recorded history, incurring several casualties and serving as a frame of reference for potential future disasters. The site is now a vast barren landscape dotted with puddles of radioactive nuclear waste, inhabited by mutated creatures such as Yao Guai, Radscorpions, and Radroaches.

Hamilton's Hideaway is a small cave in the Capital Wasteland that was originally built as an unfinished bomb shelter for a family of three who distrusted Vault-Tec. After the Great War, the network of tunnels became a hideout for chem smugglers. According to Evan King, it is one of three possible locations where a group known as The Family might reside. The cave is inhabited by various creatures such as radscorpions and radroaches, as well as raiders, and contains a hidden weapons cache.

The Jefferson Memorial is a monument in the Capital Wasteland that was selected as the site of Project Purity, an initiative led by James to convert the memorial into a water purifier capable of cleansing the river's water of radiation for use by wasteland residents. The project was abandoned after James' wife Catherine died giving birth to their child, only to be picked up again some twenty years later. The statue of Thomas Jefferson remains submerged within the center of the facility, surrounded by the purifier infrastructure built around it. The memorial contains five interior sections accessible through the gift shop doors, though the exterior is known to be patrolled by Super Mutants.

L.O.B. Enterprises was a pre-war weapons manufacturer located in Falls Church at 18527 Fairford Drive. The company secretly developed an incendiary weapon known as the Zhu-Rong v418 Chinese Pistol under a program called Project Zhu-Rong. Employees were heavily armed and trained for a potential federal invasion or nuclear exchange, even being sworn into a so-called sovereign L.O.B.

Little Lamplight is an underground settlement in the Capital Wasteland, founded on January 26, 2078, by child survivors of the Great War who were abandoned by their adult caretakers. Located within the pre-War Lamplight Caverns tourist attraction, the community is populated entirely by children under the age of 16, who exile or kill any resident who reaches their 16th birthday, referring to them as 'mungos.' The settlement is governed by an elected mayor, a position held by Robert MacCready in 2277. The children of Little Lamplight hold a deep-seated antipathy toward adults, a sentiment rooted in their community's founding, when the last remaining adult survivor left the children to fend for themselves shortly after the Great War. The settlement's layout includes the Great Chamber, which serves as the primary living area, and features structures such as the Spelunkers restaurant, the Souvenir Shop, and the Little Lamplight Office Building, which houses the medical office and school.

The MDPL-13 Power Station is a derelict power plant in the Capital Wasteland, located north-northwest of Minefield. It consists of a main derelict power plant building with three tall chimneys and a smaller power substation to the west. The main building contains a lobby, a plant floor with feral ghouls and radiation pockets, catwalks, and an office with a Glowing One. The substation contains a workbench and safe.

Mama Dolce's is a food processing plant in the Capital Wasteland, accessible through Arlington Metro Station or the Arlington Falls Church Metro in Falls Church. The facility is divided into three parts: a processed foods area, a food distribution center, and a loading yard connecting them. Despite its outward appearance as an ordinary food manufacturer, Mama Dolce's actually served as a front for Chinese intelligence and espionage operations throughout the D.C. area, a fact revealed through encrypted terminal records.

Mason Dixon Salvage is a salvage yard in the northern Capital Wasteland, located northwest of Paradise Falls and near Drowned Devil's Crossing. The site consists of two rusted metal shacks on its east and west ends, with three overturned trailers situated south of the western shack. It has been occupied as a camp by Super Mutants and their Centaur companions, making it a hazardous area for any wasteland traveler. A captive is held at the location, and a Deathclaw has been known to roam the small hill nearby.

Megaton is a fortified settlement in the Capital Wasteland built around a crater containing an undetonated atomic bomb. Founded by people denied entry to Vault 101, the town grew into a trade hub protected by walls made from scavenged aircraft debris. Lucas Simms serves as the self-appointed sheriff, while Colin Moriarty runs the local saloon and keeps tabs on town affairs. The Church of the Children of Atom worships the central bomb, and the settlement maintains contact with Vault 101 through ambassadors established during a 2241 expedition.

Metro Central, also called Metro Center, is the largest station in the Capital Wasteland's underground metro system, located beneath Washington, D.C. where the Red and White lines cross. No faction controls it; instead, feral ghouls and vicious dogs infest the tunnels. Raiders, Talon Company mercenaries, and the feral ghouls have fought several skirmishes over the station, leaving corpses and barricades throughout.

Mothership Zeta is an alien vessel orbiting Earth that is known to abduct surface dwellers using its transporter technology. The ship holds prisoners taken across centuries, including people from before the Great War and even an astronaut, many of whom are kept in cryogenic storage. Its interior includes laboratories, robotics facilities, hangars, and a bridge equipped with a powerful energy weapon. The ship is associated with the crashed alien recon craft sometimes called Recon Craft Theta found in the Capital Wasteland.

An empty residence in Megaton, known as the Empty House, sits unoccupied until its ownership is transferred. Sheriff Lucas Simms, or his son Harden Simms if the sheriff is deceased, can grant the key to this house as a reward for disarming the central atomic bomb. Once claimed, the dwelling is renamed My Megaton House. The home features a main floor lounge, kitchenette, upstairs landing, bedroom, and an additional room often occupied by a robot butler named Wadsworth.

Northwest Seneca Station is a collapsed metro station in the Capital Wasteland, situated just north of Arefu on the opposite bank of the river. According to Evan King, it is one of three possible locations where the group known as The Family might be living. The station's accessible sections include a mole rat-infested restroom area and a converted maintenance room serving as a lab for a ghoul named Murphy and his assistant Barrett. An irradiated sewer tunnel leads from the station through the Meresti Service Tunnel to Meresti Metro Station, where The Family maintains their hideout.

Oasis is a lush, forested settlement hidden inside a large rock formation in the northern Capital Wasteland, northwest of the Clifftop Shacks. It is built upon an extensive network of caves that once sheltered survivors from a nearby mining town during the Great War. The vegetation is the result of Harold, a mutated wanderer who had a tree named Herbert, or Bob, growing from his body. Harold took root here roughly 20 to 30 years ago, and his mutation spread seed pods that spawned the surrounding trees, grass, and plants.

The Olney Sewers are a small sewer system beneath Old Olney in the Capital Wasteland. Like the town above, the sewers are infested with Deathclaws, making them extremely dangerous to explore. The tunnels contain a maintenance room with a terminal connected to a Protectron unit, and a partly collapsed section where the body of a Brotherhood of Steel Initiate can be found. Some areas of the sewer connect to deeper underground passages beneath Old Olney.

Our Lady of Hope Hospital is a ruined medical facility located near Vernon Square Station in the Capital Wasteland. The building has been overrun by Super Mutants, who gather there in concentrated numbers while searching for traces of the Forced Evolutionary Virus once used at Vault 87. A fallen broadcasting antenna connects the hospital to the Statesman Hotel, serving as a bridge to the hotel's upper floors. The hospital contains numerous traps and a significant stockpile of medical supplies, including blood packs and copies of D.C.

Paradise Falls is a fortified slaver compound built from the ruins of a pre-War strip mall, recognizable by its Large Boy statue landmark. The slave trade here has been led by figures such as Harmon Jurley and Penelope Chase, with Eulogy Jones currently managing operations after killing the previous leader. The compound includes slaver barracks, a weapons shop, a clinic, and holding pens where captives are bought, sold, and stored. Herbert Dashwood notes that the slaving operations were once less organized but have since made Paradise Falls the most dangerous dump in the Capital Wasteland.

Point Lookout is a desolate, swampy region downriver from the Capital Wasteland that was never directly hit by nuclear bombs but suffered severe irradiation from the Potomac River. The pervasive radiation in its bogs led to the evolution of the Swampfolk, crazed and highly deformed people who inhabit the swamps alongside Feral Ghouls and Swamplurks. Almost entirely devoid of organized society, the area is sparsely populated by a few isolated individuals like Tobar the Ferryman and local Tribals. It is known to outsiders primarily for its unique Punga Fruit and the legends of hidden pre-War technology scattered among its abandoned buildings and Civil War-era mass graves.

Reclining Groves Resort Homes is a ruined pre-War neighborhood in the Capital Wasteland, situated north of Germantown Police HQ and west-northwest of the MDPL-13 Power Station. The area consists of seven destroyed houses and a small playground lining a stretch of paved road. A scavenger and his dog have set up a makeshift shop in a partially destroyed barn on the eastern end of the settlement. A dirt path leading south from the barn up a small hill leads to Warren, a small cave home to vicious dogs and the corpses of a mercenary and a wastelander.

topic_desc_basic: The Republic of Dave is a small farming community in the northeastern Capital Wasteland, east of Old Olney, founded on the site of a pre-War separatist militia compound. Over its history, the settlement has been known by many names, including the Kingdom of Larry, the Republic of Stevie-Ray, Billsylvania, the New Republic of Stevie-Ray, and most recently the Kingdom of Tom, before its current ruler Dave took control from his father Tom and reformed it into the Republic of Dave. The compound consists of a single extended family living among several buildings, including a capitol, a museum, a school, and a tourism office, and is governed by Dave, who insists on being addressed as Mr. President.

Rivet City is the largest settlement in the Capital Wasteland, housed within a decaying pre-war aircraft carrier grounded in Washington, D.C. It was formally established in 2239 by Horace Pinkerton, Annette Holmes, and Brad Danvers, growing from a naval science outpost into a thriving community governed by a three-person council representing scientists, civilians, and security personnel. The city is renowned for its hydroponic farms that produce non-irradiated food, its advanced science lab, and a well-equipped security force trained by veterans like Harkness and Lana Danvers. Challenges facing the settlement include respiratory ailments caused by rust, social tensions between upper deck and hangar deck residents, and the constant need to defend against raiders, super mutants, and mirelurks that infest the ship's lower sections.

The RobCo Facility is a pre-war RobCo Industries factory located in the Capital Wasteland, northeast of Tenpenny Tower and southwest of Fort Independence. It was used for the assembly of Protectron robots, with many units left dormant in charging stations throughout the building. By 2277, the facility is infested with mole rats and radroaches, and its production mainframe remains operational, capable of issuing commands to the robots and turrets within. A traveling robot merchant known as Tinker Joe can occasionally be found in the parking lot outside, accompanied by his automatons, including a military-grade Protectron designated Sergeant RL-3.

The Robot Repair Center is a facility in the Capital Wasteland situated south-southwest of Canterbury Commons. Before the Great War, the building operated as a large discount electronics warehouse known as Darren's Discounts. In the post-nuclear era, the structure has been repurposed as the base of the Mechanist, a wasteland figure who uses robots to enforce his vision of order. The interior is divided into office spaces, two automated repair sectors, and a secret lair known as the Mechanist's Forge, all heavily guarded by Protectrons, Sentry Bots, and automated turrets.

Shalebridge is a location in the Capital Wasteland situated north of Broadcast Tower KT8 and southwest of the Abandoned Car Fort. It consists of a broken relay tower, the Shalebridge tunnels, and Shalebridge Hill, with the latter two areas serving as homes to rival ant colonies. The Shalebridge Tunnels, marked by green mushrooms, house a small colony of passive mutated forager ants, while Shalebridge Hill, surrounded by golden fungus, contains an aggressive colony of giant worker ants, soldier ants, and a giant ant queen. The tunnels also hold the remains of an ant researcher found in a pool of water near the egg clusters, along with the bodies of raiders who perished in the area.

The Statesman Hotel is a twelve-story building located in Vernon Square within the ruins of Washington, D.C. Before the Great War, it catered to upper-class clientele, but it is now infested with Super Mutants and Centaurs. The majority of the hotel is only accessible by traveling through Our Lady of Hope Hospital and crossing a fallen radio mast. The mercenary group known as Reilly's Rangers is stranded on the hotel's rooftop, pinned down by Super Mutant forces.

Taft Tunnel is an escape route leading from the Jefferson Memorial to a sewer grate outside The Citadel, situated just south of the west point of Key Bridge. The tunnel system is infested with feral ghouls and contains numerous radioactive barrels. Further inside, the passages branch into areas occupied by Enclave soldiers and a Brotherhood of Steel paladin wielding a flamer. The route ultimately leads up a ladder to the entrance of The Citadel.

Tenpenny Tower is a fortified settlement in the Capital Wasteland, located west of the DC ruins and southwest of the RobCo Facility. Before the Great War, the structure served as a resort for the wealthy and powerful, built on the foundations of an old plantation. By 2277, the tower had become a private, elitist residential and commercial building under the ownership of Allistair Tenpenny, an English entrepreneur who only permitted the well-to-do to reside there while strictly barring Ghouls from entry. Tenpenny hired individuals to repair and secure the building, including Chief Gustavo, who heads security, and his right-hand man Mister Burke.

The Citadel, sometimes called the DC Bunker, is the headquarters of the Brotherhood of Steel in the Capital Wasteland and occupies the ruins of the former Pentagon at the west end of the Key Bridge. The Brotherhood arrived in the area in 2255 and established their headquarters within the first few months, discovering a pre-War robotic super weapon named Liberty Prime inside the building, which they began to repair. From this location, the Brotherhood searched for advanced technology hidden in the capital's ruins, with the facility's new construction led by Scribe Bowditch. Enclave President John Henry Eden has declared on Enclave Radio that the facility is the country's most important military installation and labeled the Brotherhood criminals with the audacity to claim it as their own personal clubhouse.

The Mall is a bombed-out war zone in Washington, D.C., occupied by Super Mutants. The well-maintained public park has been replaced by a network of trenches, fences, and bunkers in fortified positions where the Super Mutants are located. Crossing this part of the Mall will involve enduring firefights unless sneaking around the outsides, but the underground metro stations on either side of this zone bypass the conflict. The outside of Underworld is patrolled by Willow, who, despite her claims that Super Mutants leave ghouls alone, will be shot at by nearby Super Mutants.

The Pitt is a Raider-dominated city built in the ruins of Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. After the Great War, local gangs took over the area, and diseases such as Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion turned much of the populace into hostile creatures like Trogs and Wildmen. The Brotherhood of Steel, led by Paladin Lyons, swept through the city in a single night during an operation known as The Scourge, wiping out hostiles and departing with around twenty healthy children to be initiated into the Brotherhood. Initiate Ishmael Ashur, presumed dead and buried in rubble during The Scourge, survived and established himself as leader of The Pitt, rebuilding its industry and steel mills using slave labor.

Underworld is a ghoul settlement established within the Museum of History in the Capital Wasteland, taking its name from a pre-war exhibit on death and the afterlife whose banners still hang at the entrance. In the days following the Great War, survivors who sheltered in the museum gradually transformed into ghouls, with some losing their minds and the rest accepting their fate and building a community. Over the years the settlement grew to include businesses such as Carol's Place, The Ninth Circle bar, Underworld Outfitters, and Doctor Barrows' clinic, and the ghouls there made contact with other ghoul communities as far away as Appalachia. The inhabitants are wary of outsiders but welcoming to well-behaved visitors, resent the Brotherhood of Steel for stirring up conflict in the area, and are notably unbothered by the super mutants camped across the road on the National Mall.

Vault 101 is a Vault-Tec shelter located northwest of Megaton and west of Springvale in the Capital Wasteland. Overseen by Alphonse Almodovar, the Vault's inhabitants have remained largely isolated from the outside world, with the Overseer maintaining strict control over the population. The Vault is divided into four sections: the main entrance, overseer's tunnel, atrium/upper level, and lower level, each serving different functions for the community. Vault 101 did not receive a G.E.C.K. and its genetic diversity is only able to sustain the population for a few more generations.

Vault 112 is a Vault-Tec Vault located in the southwestern Capital Wasteland, beneath Smith Casey's Garage. Constructed between 2068 and 2074, it was designed for only 85 occupants who were to be suspended indefinitely in a virtual reality simulation. The Vault was built to serve the needs of its Overseer, Dr. Stanislaus Braun, the creator of the Garden of Eden Creation Kit. Braun installed a virtual reality simulator with VR pods containing several simulated worlds, the last of which is the Tranquility Lane Simulation.

Vault 87 is a Vault-Tec installation in the Capital Wasteland, located northwest of Little Lamplight. Construction began in May 2066 and finished in December 2071, with the vault equipped with a General Atomics nuclear reactor, a backup Versicorps fusion power generator, four stasis chambers, a plasma containment field, six food processing stations, and a Garden of Eden Creation Kit. Under Dr. Wayne Merrick, the staff studied the effects of the Forced Evolutionary Virus on humans as part of the Evolutionary Experimentation Program, with the Overseer and security guards aware of the experimentation.

The Washington Monument is a pre-War obelisk standing at the center of the Mall in the Capital Wasteland. The Brotherhood of Steel has claimed the structure as an outpost because it houses the signal transmitter for Galaxy News Radio. A unit called the 2nd Monument Defense Detachment, led by Paladin Berrings, guards the location and its surrounding perimeter. The Brotherhood insignia is stenciled on the entrance doors, and the tall monument is visible from nearly anywhere in the wasteland.

The Yao Guai Tunnels are a cave system in the Capital Wasteland situated west of the Charnel House and northwest of Smith Casey's Garage, with an entrance set into a rocky outcrop behind a chain-link fence door. As the name suggests, the tunnels are home to a large number of Yao Guai, with a roughly circular den chamber forming the heart of their habitat. Several Wastelanders have attempted to make a home in these caves at one time or another, leaving behind mattresses, cooking implements, ammunition containers, and various other personal effects. The tunnels consist of a fairly straightforward central intersection with a few smaller dead-end branches, and the den can be reached by following the eastern passages of the cave system.

The 188 Trading Post is a commercial outpost at the intersection of Highway 93 and Highway 95 in the Mojave Wasteland, north of El Dorado Dry Lake and west-northwest of Boulder City. It was established shortly before the Courier's arrival by Samuel Kerr and his daughter Michelle, traders from Primm who fled after the NCRCF prison break unleashed escaped convicts into the city. Recognizing the increased traffic flowing up Highway 95 toward New Vegas due to the closure of I-15, combined with regular NCR troop movements between Hoover Dam and Camp McCarran, they set up the 188 Slop & Shop, offering food, water, supplies, and repair services under the motto "It's Better Than Nothing." The post quickly attracted other vendors, including an independent Arms Merchant selling from her truck and Alexander, who operates a satellite location for the Gun Runners beneath the overpass. A young boy known as the Forecaster also sits nearby, selling thoughts to passersby.

The Atomic Wrangler Casino is a casino in Freeside, situated across the street from the Silver Rush on the pre-War Fremont Street. It is owned by the twins Francine and James Garret. The Atomic Wrangler, the only active casino in Freeside (featuring a neon sign of a futuristic cowboy riding a stylized atom), is also a flophouse, brothel, and source of chems, located just down the main drag. It is run by the Garret twins, protected by their thugs, and is a common hangout for the Van Graffs and the Kings.

Big MT, also called the Big MT Research Facility or the Big Empty, was a pre-War scientific research center and defense contractor located south of Hopeville. It drew some of the brightest minds of the twenty-first century, producing advances in sonic emitters, space age alloys, DNA hybridization, force fields, and Auto-Doc surgery. The facility was built beneath a mountain and included a concentration camp called Little Yangtze, where Chinese citizens and suspected Communist infiltrators were held and used as research subjects with total pacification collars. After the Great War, the site was damaged and its dome exposed within a crater, and an event known as the Great Static caused further destruction.

Black Mountain is a former pre-War Hermes Communications monitoring station in the Mojave Wasteland, topped by a satellite array that tracked Chinese satellite activity before the Great War. During the war, operators recorded multiple launches from both sides before the facility's staff succumbed to radiation, though the mountain shielded the broadcast tower itself. After the war, Marcus and a group of Super Mutants settled there, finding the array still operational and the mountain defensible. One inhabitant, Tabitha, began broadcasting on Black Mountain Radio, and the resulting disagreements fractured the group, leading Marcus and his followers to depart for Jacobstown.

Boulder City is a small town in the Mojave Wasteland situated west of Hoover Dam and southeast of the 188 Trading Post. The town survived the Great War intact but was largely destroyed in 2277 during the First Battle of Hoover Dam, when NCR forces under Chief Hanlon's command lured Caesar's Legion into the town and detonated explosives packed throughout it, breaking the Legion's offensive at the cost of the settlement itself. The Boulder City Memorial stands near the western entrance, honoring the NCR troopers who fell in the battle. In the years since, the ruins became a stopover for caravans and a source of concrete for NCR fortifications along the Colorado River, using limestone shipped by train from Quarry Junction.

California is the name of a pre-War American state whose legacy persists long after the Great War. The region is widely known as the heartland of the New California Republic, often called New California or NCR territory, and figures prominently in trade, politics, and military affairs across the post-War West. The Crimson Caravan Company, one of the largest trading outfits operating out of California, maintains extensive business operations there, and wealthy families such as the Jamisons of Redding invest heavily in its commerce. The Brotherhood of Steel has a long history in California, where it first encountered the Enclave decades ago, and the Enclave itself once maintained hidden bases and a headquarters off the California coast.

Camp Forlorn Hope, sometimes shortened to "Hope," is a New California Republic Army main camp on the banks of the Colorado River south of Hoover Dam. The camp was established around a water source and consists of a ramshackle collection of tents, shacks, and salvaged buses divided by a creek. After Camp Searchlight fell and Legion forces overran the NCR outpost at Nelson, Camp Forlorn Hope found itself on the front line, with morale at an all-time low and ranks depleted by ongoing skirmishes in the no man's land between the two positions. Major Polatli commands the camp and blames the army's highest commanders for the mismanagement, though he has prepared plans to increase troop numbers, restore supply lines, and retake Nelson to secure the army's flank for the inevitable battle at the dam.

Camp Guardian is a New California Republic Army outpost under construction on Guardian Peak in the Mojave Wasteland, positioned to overlook the Colorado River and intercept Legion forces. A squad led by Sergeant Banner was dispatched to establish the fortification, but they soon suffered from supply shortages and strange noises reported by the soldiers. The troops eventually discovered a cave system near their camp that was missed by the initial survey team. The camp was subsequently overrun by lakelurks emerging from the caves, leaving Private Halford as the only known survivor to broadcast a distress signal.

Camp McCarran, formerly known as McCarran International Airport, is a pre-War airport that serves as the headquarters for the New California Republic Army in the Mojave Wasteland. Located south of the New Vegas Strip, the base is a major hub for troop allocation, supply distribution, and military intelligence. The NCR established a presence there as part of the Treaty of New Vegas, utilizing its pre-War fortifications and direct monorail connection to the Strip. Under the command of Colonel James Hsu, the garrison is the largest in the area and is constantly engaged in skirmishes with the Fiends while dealing with infiltrations by Caesar's Legion spies.

Camp Searchlight is an irradiated former NCR military camp located at the intersection of Nevada 164 and Highway 95 in the Mojave Wasteland. Originally a Pre-War gold mining town, it became contaminated when trucks carrying nuclear waste from San Onofre were diverted there during the Great War. The New California Republic later established a sizable military base at the site, which posed a significant obstacle to Caesar's Legion due to its strategic location. Rather than mounting a direct assault, Vulpes Inculta exploited gaps in the NCR patrol schedule and sent recruit legionaries to open the nuclear waste containers, irradiating the entire area and rendering it unusable as a military installation.

Cottonwood Cove is a former resort along the Colorado River in the Mojave Wasteland that Caesar's Legion adopted as a staging area and outpost. It serves as a hub for trafficking captured people to Arizona for slave processing and as a launching point for Legion raiding operations in the southern Mojave. After Vulpes Inculta destroyed Camp Searchlight, the NCR's presence in the region waned and the Legion established Cottonwood Cove as their largest encampment on the western bank of the Colorado. Centurion Aurelius of Phoenix commands the camp with two contubernia, and all communication to and from the cove is handled via ham radio.

Freeside is a slum located directly adjacent to the New Vegas Strip, situated around the intersection of pre-War Fremont Street and Las Vegas Boulevard. Mr. House directed tribes to build the crude outer walls that separate it from the rest of New Vegas, later building a second inner wall to use Freeside as a filter for undesirables he did not want on the Strip. The district is ruled by the Kings and the Van Graffs, with the Followers of the Apocalypse operating out of the Old Mormon Fort to help with the community's basic needs.

Gomorrah Hotel and Casino is a prominent establishment on the New Vegas Strip, managed by the Omertas under the oversight of Mr. House, whom they refer to as "the Overboss" or "Not-At-Home." Unlike other casinos that offer a refined atmosphere, Gomorrah openly embraces vice, offering gambling, alcohol, chems, and prostitution. It is uniquely ghoul-friendly, employing ghoul bartenders and prostitutes while offering its services to ghoul patrons. The casino features the Brimstone lounge, a courtyard for soliciting, and the exclusive Zoara Club where the Omerta leadership, Nero and Big Sal, conduct their business.

Goodsprings is a small mining town in the Mojave Wasteland, named after the Goodsprings Source that supplies its water. It was settled after the Great War with a grant from the New California Republic to develop a mining operation near the water source. The town is built around Nevada 160 and includes a saloon, general store, schoolhouse, and Doc Mitchell's house. Recently, trade has declined due to a prison break at the NCR Correctional Facility and a Deathclaw infestation at Quarry Junction shutting down I-15.

HELIOS One is a pre-War Poseidon Energy concentrated solar power plant in the Mojave Wasteland that secretly housed the control systems for the experimental ARCHIMEDES orbital weapons. The Brotherhood of Steel occupied the facility for years under Father Elijah until they were driven out by the New California Republic during Operation: Sunburst in 2276. As of 2281, the NCR maintains a firm foothold at the plant, though it remains barely operational under the supervision of an incompetent engineer known as Fantastic. A representative of the Followers of the Apocalypse, Ignacio Rivas, is also stationed at the facility to research its secrets and ensure its weapon systems remain undiscovered.

Hidden Valley is a fenced-in former USAF testing range in the Mojave Wasteland, located northeast of the NCR Correctional Facility and southeast of Sloan. The valley contains four bunkers spread around its perimeter, with the west bunker serving as the home of the Mojave chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel, who retreated there after being defeated by the NCR at HELIOS One during Operation: Sunburst. The area is protected by the DERVISH camouflage system, a cloaking mechanism that makes targeting the site impossible for automated systems and generates a sandstorm each evening. Prospectors have reported seeing armored figures emerging from the valley during these storms, though the bunker intercoms typically garner no response.

The Hidden Valley Bunker is a location in the Mojave Wasteland situated southeast of Sloan, serving as the home of the Brotherhood of Steel. It is protected by a pre-War DERVISH camouflage system that cloaks the bunkers and makes automated targeting impossible. The facility is divided into two main levels containing personnel quarters, an armory, a medical bay, a workshop, and virtual reality chambers surrounding the main reactor. The bunker is led by Elder McNamara and Head Paladin Hardin, with scribes and knights occupying the archives and machine shop on the second floor.

Higgs Village is a location within the Big MT research facility that consists of a warehouse containing six houses arranged around a central fountain. Each house is numbered and formerly belonged to one of the Think Tank scientists, including Doctor 0, Doctor Klein, Doctor Mobius, Doctor Borous, Doctor Dala, and Doctor 8. The layout strongly resembles Tranquility Lane, suggesting it was used for some form of experiment or testing by the pre-War researchers. The residences contain various personal effects of the scientists, such as Doctor Borous's dog house for his dog Gabe and Doctor Dala's abundance of teddy bears.

Hoover Dam, often called the Old World Wall, is a massive hydroelectric dam on the Colorado River that survived the Great War in almost untouched condition thanks to Mr. House's defense systems. After centuries of abandonment, the New California Republic occupied the structure in 2274 and later signed the Treaty of New Vegas, securing 95 percent of its power output while guaranteeing the sovereignty of New Vegas. In 2277, Caesar's Legion attempted to seize the dam but was defeated by NCR forces during the First Battle of Hoover Dam.

Jacobstown is a pre-War resort on Mount Charleston northwest of New Vegas, now serving as a super mutant settlement founded by Marcus, the former sheriff of Broken Hills. Marcus left Black Mountain with a splinter group of super mutants and renamed the resort after an old friend, intending to build a peaceful community open to all so long as they remain nonviolent. The settlement is home to super mutants, nightkin led by Keene, and a sizable bighorner population that provides food and trade goods. Doctor Henry and Calamity are working on a cure for the mental illness afflicting the nightkin, though progress is slow and the nightkin grow restless.

The King's School of Impersonation is a three-story building in Freeside at the intersection of Fremont Street and Las Vegas Boulevard, serving as the headquarters of the Kings gang and their leader, known simply as The King. Before the Great War, the business operated as an impersonation school, and the gang members continue this tradition by emulating the original "king" while ruling as the predominant power in Freeside. The building features a reception area, a theater with a stage where gang members perform for The King, and multiple floors of bedrooms, recreation rooms, and storage areas. A chalkboard on the third floor bears a "King Impersonation Checklist" with instructions to move hips, say "uh huh," say "momma," and prepare peanut butter and banana sandwiches.

The Lucky 38 Resort and Casino is the most prominent structure on the New Vegas Strip, serving as both a pre-War relic and a symbol of Mr. House's vision for Las Vegas. Before the Great War, Mr. House extensively modified the building with long-range laser cannons to intercept nuclear warheads and constructed a concealed chamber to serve as his life support system.

The Lucky 38 Presidential Suite, also referred to as the High Roller Suite by Victor, is a luxurious accommodation located within the Lucky 38 casino in New Vegas. The suite features a master bedroom, a guest room, a kitchen, a bathroom, and a recreation room. It serves as a clubhouse for companions, who can be dismissed to this location and will engage in various activities such as wandering, sitting, sleeping, drinking, eating, and interacting with one another. The recreation room houses a pool table, a television, and the Snow Globe Stand, while the kitchen contains a long table, two ovens, and a refrigerator.

Mick & Ralph's is an active consumable and gun shop located in the Freeside slum area of New Vegas, just northeast of the east gate. The business is operated by two colleagues, with Mick selling weapons and Ralph handling consumables and special services. They provide fine quality trinkets to discerning customers while serving the local riff-raff low-grade armaments from the seedier side of Freeside. The building's sign originally only read Ralph's, with the Mick & portion added by the duo after the Great War when they began using the building.

NCR Ranger Outpost Mojave, commonly called Mojave Outpost, sits near the California-Nevada state line along Interstate 15 and serves as the gateway to the Mojave Wasteland for caravans traveling from the New California Republic's core lands. Established in 2249, it functions as a military hub and administrative command center for operations in the southwestern Mojave, with soldiers acting as border guards to protect trade routes. The outpost is marked by the Unification Monument, commemorating the 2271 Ranger Unification Treaty that merged the Desert Rangers of Nevada with the NCR Rangers against the threat of Caesar's Legion. By 2281, the outpost struggles with reduced patrols and backed-up caravans following the NCRCF prison break, leaving anxious soldiers worried that if Legion forces push past Nipton, the outpost itself could become the frontline.

The Mojave Wasteland, synonymous with the pre-War Mojave Desert, spans portions of California, Nevada, and Arizona. Thanks to intricate defense systems established by Mr. House, the region survived the Great War relatively unscathed, leaving much of its infrastructure and technology intact. By 2281, the region is locked in a delicate balance of power between the expanding New California Republic, the encroaching forces of Caesar's Legion, and the independent Free Economic Zone of New Vegas.

The NCR Correctional Facility, also known as the NCRCF, is a former prison southeast of Goodsprings that was operated by the New California Republic as a labor camp where inmates maintained the regional railways. Originally the Jean Conservancy, a low-security all-female prison, the facility fell to a prisoner uprising organized by an inmate named Samuel Cooke, who stockpiled blast powder and makeshift weapons. Following the breakout, many of the escaped convicts, who came to be known as Powder Gangers, scattered across the surrounding wasteland while the remainder stayed behind under the leadership of a man named Eddie. The facility is watched with interest by the Brotherhood of Steel, which keeps scouts posted nearby.

The NCR Sharecropper Farms are an agricultural settlement located directly south of Freeside's East Gate in the Mojave Wasteland. Established under the Thaler Act, private farmers cultivate the land for the New California Republic in exchange for military protection, housing, food, and water, with a portion of the crop yield going to NCR military locations such as Camp McCarran and Hoover Dam. Irrigation water is pumped from Lake Mead through a pipe system, with the Office of Science and Industry at Camp McCarran pre-calculating optimal water usage for each crop. A military unit is stationed on-site at all times to deter theft.

Nellis Air Force Base, also known as the Nellis homeland, is a heavily fortified location northeast of New Vegas in the Mojave Wasteland. Once the United States Air Force Warfare Center, the base was struck by nuclear weapons during the Great War and left highly radioactive and abandoned for decades. The Boomers, a group that originally inhabited Vault 34, eventually settled there and made it their home, using the base's remaining defenses and their own heavy arms to keep strangers away. The base is largely self-sufficient, with irrigated crops, solar power, a biodiesel refinery, and medical and educational facilities, while the Boomers train in virtual reality stations in hopes of one day returning to the skies.

Nelson is a settlement in the Mojave Wasteland, located southwest of Camp Forlorn Hope and east of Novac. Originally occupied by the New California Republic as a strategic military camp between Camp Forlorn Hope and Camp Searchlight, it was attacked and captured by Caesar's Legion under Decanus Dead Sea shortly after the NCR occupation. The town has remained under Legion control, with Dead Sea executing captured NCR troopers to demoralize surrounding forces and launching raids against Camp Forlorn Hope.

New Vegas, built on the remains of pre-War Las Vegas in the Mojave Desert, is managed by the reclusive Mr. House and his army of Securitron robots. Having predicted the Great War, House defended the city with laser cannons and disarm codes, sparing the main city from nuclear devastation before falling into a coma for decades. Upon waking, he rebuilt the New Vegas Strip with the help of recruited tribals known as the Three Families, completing renovations in 2274 just before NCR forces entered the region, leading to the Treaty of New Vegas that granted him sovereignty over the Strip.

The New Vegas Strip is the rebuilt heart of New Vegas, restored by Robert House with the help of Securitrons and the Three Families in 2274 before NCR forces entered the region. The Treaty of New Vegas granted House sovereignty over the Strip while allowing NCR soldiers and civilians to visit its casinos and establishments, with the NCR forbidden from annexing it by force due to the Legion threat. Powered by electricity from Hoover Dam, the Strip features several reopened pre-War establishments and serves as a major draw for tourism, with NCR citizens described by House as a society of customers desperate for comfort and luxury. Entrance to the Strip is guarded by Securitrons who require visitors to demonstrate sufficient wealth or possess a New Vegas Passport.

Nipton is a small town in the southern Mojave Wasteland, located near the Nevada-California state line and transected by railroad tracks. Before the Great War, the town was known for hosting a lottery that offered a jackpot worth millions of dollars. After the war, Nipton was led by Mayor Joseph B. Steyn, who attempted to maintain peace between NCR soldiers and Powder Gangers by inviting each group at different times of day.

Novac is an independent town along Highway 95 in the Mojave Wasteland, named after the broken motel sign at its entrance. Before the Great War, it was a small roadside stopover featuring the Dinky the Dinosaur novelty attraction and the World's 2nd Largest Thermometer, catering to travelers heading to the nearby REPCONN Test Site. After the war, settlers reclaimed the motel and surrounding area, establishing a modest community sustained by salvage from the REPCONN site and trade along the highway. The town is guarded by two NCR Army veterans, Craig Boone and Manny Vargas, who use the Dinky the T-Rex statue as a sniper's nest, while retired Ranger Andy also contributes to its defense.

Primm, sometimes called "budget Vegas" or "the other New Vegas," is an independent settlement in the Mojave Wasteland located alongside Interstate 15 in Clark County, Nevada. Before the Great War, it was a small resort town featuring attractions like the Vikki and Vance Casino and the Bison Steve Casino and Hotel. As the New California Republic expanded into the Mojave, it became a promising trade town until a recent breakout of prisoners from the NCR Correctional Facility put an end to commerce. The escaped convicts, known as Powder Gangers, took over the center of town, forcing the residents to seek refuge in the Vikki and Vance Casino while the NCR's 5th Battalion watches from afar, lacking the numbers to reclaim the strategic location.

Puesta del Sol is a district of the Villa surrounding the Sierra Madre, divided into northern and southern sections. Its construction crews frequently clashed with the casino construction crews, and the district's development lagged behind that of its sister district, Salida del Sol, as if the effort had simply run out of steam and money. Much of the ground level is choked by the toxic red Cloud, though a ventilation system in the Puesta del Sol Switching Station can clear much of it. The area is infested with Ghost People and littered with bear traps, radios, and speakers that can detonate collars or summon further threats.

REPCONN Headquarters in Henderson, Nevada, served as the home office of REPCONN Aerospace, formally known as the Rocket Engineering and Production Company of Nevada, a firm specializing in rocket manufacture. RobCo Industries acquired the company and overhauled the building with heightened security measures, including automatic facial recognition monitors, badge scanners, security locks, and heavily armed sentry bots, to support classified research operations. Employees were required to wear identification badges at all times, and the third floor was restricted to executives who needed a daily password for access. The facility was the site of a plasma rifle project that produced the Q-35 Matter Modulator, the first working prototype of its kind.

Ranger Station Charlie is a New California Republic Rangers stronghold in the central Mojave Wasteland, converted from the pre-War Shady Pines trailer park. Located southwest of Novac along a railroad track, the station provides the rangers with a safehouse and helps establish territorial control over the southeastern sector of the Mojave, a role that became especially important after the fall of Camp Searchlight. The trailers have been piled up to create a makeshift fortress, with the communications center and barracks set up in the old trailer park office building. The commanding officer is Ranger Beaumont, but he and most of his command are typically out on patrol, leaving Comm Officer Stepinac to watch over the encampment.

Salida del Sol is the eastern section of the Villa surrounding the Sierra Madre, originally built to house a church and the homes of many casino staff before the Great War. The district is divided into northern and southern halves, both heavily littered with traps and mines often hidden within the toxic Cloud. It is infested with a large number of Ghost People, and navigation is complicated by blocked gates, locked doors, and the ever-present haze. The Salida Switching Station sits in the southwest corner and contains a terminal capable of restoring power to the ventilation system to clear the Cloud from the area.

The Sierra Madre is a legendary pre-War casino resort and adjoining villa designed by Frederick Sinclair as both a luxurious retreat and a shelter from nuclear holocaust, where guests could reverse their fortunes and begin again. Surrounded by a poisonous Cloud born of experimental technologies supplied by Big MT, the isolated location has lured countless prospectors through a mysterious radio broadcast advertising its Gala Event, though none have returned. The resort was designed for total self-sufficiency, with unique vending machines providing all necessities to inhabitants cut off from the outside world, while a small but well-equipped human security force guarded the grounds alongside holographic defenders.

The Silver Rush is a location in Freeside on Fremont Street, opposite the Atomic Wrangler Casino. Established in 2071, it originally rivaled the Atomic Wrangler as a casino before the Van Graff family killed its former occupants and took over. When the Kings protested, the Van Graffs reduced several of their members to goo, and the two groups have left each other alone ever since. Now the largest retailer of energy weapons in the Mojave Wasteland, the Silver Rush is headed by Gloria Van Graff and Jean-Baptiste Cutting, after Frieda Van Graff departed to pursue personal interests.

The Sunset Sarsaparilla Headquarters was the pre-War corporate office and bottling center for the Sunset Sarsaparilla Company in Las Vegas. Located northwest of the El Rey Motel and west of the NCR Sharecropper Farms, it is one of the largest buildings in the area and features a distinctive entrance shaped like a giant bottle. The facility housed corporate offices, a regional bottling and distribution center, and a staff of security protectrons and maintenance robots. A cowboy robot named Festus stands near the entrance, where he promotes a promotional contest involving Sunset Sarsaparilla Star Bottle Caps.

The Divide is a stretch of devastated land in the northwestern Mojave Wasteland near the California-Nevada border, once home to the pre-war towns of Hopeville and Ashton. Both communities were built above an extensive network of nuclear missile silos managed by the Commonwealth Defense Administration, situated in a geologically unstable region where earthquakes were common. After the Great War, the settlements grew into a thriving community connected to the outside world by a courier who regularly traveled the supply road, and the name Divide referred to this route from the west into the Mojave rather than to the land itself. Before the first Battle of Hoover Dam, a package delivered by a courier contained a detonator that activated the underground warheads, triggering a massive earthquake that ripped the land open and unleashed constant dust storms, killing or maiming soldiers from both the NCR and Caesar's Legion and turning them into skinless Marked Men healed by radiation.

Fortification Hill, commonly known as The Fort, is the primary base of Caesar's Legion situated on the east bank of the Colorado River. Established in 2277, it serves as the staging ground where Caesar and his Praetorian Guards prepare for a second assault on the NCR at Hoover Dam. The camp is built above Mr. House's secret bunker, which is concealed within a pre-existing weather monitoring station.

The Sink is a facility located at the top of the Big MT dome in the Big Mountain research center. Originally owned by Doctor Mobius, it served as a testbed for several personality subroutines embedded in its appliances and fixtures. Mobius removed the personality chips, disabling many of the various functions of its modules, and after a heated argument with Mobius, Doctor Klein took the chips and tossed them off the Sink's balcony. Various staff members working in Big Mountain later recovered the chips and stored them in different areas of the facility.

The Tops Hotel and Casino is a mainstay of the New Vegas Strip, restored to its pre-War glory by Mr. House and the Chairmen. Formerly the Boot Riders tribe, the Chairmen adopted a stylish, classic Vegas persona to run the establishment, offering gambling, food, and entertainment. The casino's legendary Aces Theater, managed by Tommy Torini, constantly attracts fresh talent from across the wasteland.

The Ultra-Luxe Las Vegas Resort is a luxurious pre-War casino and resort located on the New Vegas Strip. It is operated by the White Glove Society, one of the Three Families recruited by Mr. House to manage the Strip's casinos. The society's members are known for being well-dressed and well-spoken, maintaining an air of high class.

Vault 11 is an abandoned Vault-Tec installation in the Mojave Wasteland, situated west of Boulder City and southwest of the 188 Trading Post. Its social experiment required dwellers to sacrifice one member annually or face total extermination by the vault mainframe, making the position of overseer synonymous with death. Over time, political factions called voting blocs formed to influence the selection process, including the Justice Bloc, Human Dignity Bloc, Divine Will Bloc, Allied Service Workers Bloc, United Vault Technicians Bloc, and Utilitarian Bloc, with the Coalition of Vault 11 Voting Blocs providing oversight. Corruption festered as bloc leaders manipulated elections through bribery, drug trafficking, and coercion, culminating in violence after Overseer Katherine Stone dissolved the election process in Overseer Order 745.

Vault 19 is a Vault-Tec installation in the Mojave Wasteland, concealed beneath a sewer grate in an abandoned parking lot along Nevada 159 northeast of Goodsprings. The vault's experiment divided inhabitants into red and blue sectors under two separate overseers, inducing paranoia through subliminal messaging, unusual drafts, and blinking light patterns while each faction blamed the other for mounting malfunctions and psychosis. By the time escaped convicts from the NCR Correctional Facility discovered it, the original population was gone entirely. Samuel Cooke, founder of the Powder Gangers, now occupies the vault with his own followers, though his men are not considered part of that faction.

Vault 21 is a Vault-Tec vault located in downtown Las Vegas that was successfully converted into a hotel and casino. Its original social experiment required perfect equality among its inhabitants, with a symmetrical layout and all conflicts resolved through games of chance. After Mr. House contacted the vault dwellers with an offer to join the resurrection of New Vegas, a lengthy game of Blackjack determined that the vault would open to the outside world.

Vault 22 is a Vault-Tec installation in the Mojave Wasteland, located east of Jacobstown and west of the Thorn. Before the Great War, it was populated by scientists dedicated to agricultural research, developing advanced fertilizers and pest control agents like the Beauveria Mordicana fungus. After the war, the fungus became airborne and infected the vault's population, turning them into Spore Carriers. In 2096, a group of infected survivors known as the Coughers arrived in Zion Canyon, where they were wiped out by Randall Clark.

Vault 3 is a control Vault in the South Vegas Ruins of the Mojave Wasteland, built by Vault-Tec without an experiment. Its original dwellers opened the Vault after a water leak in the 23rd century and traded with outsiders, but the Fiends exploited their naivety, killed them, and claimed the Vault as a fortress and drug den. The Fiends, led by Motor-Runner, use Vault 3 as a base to threaten southwestern New Vegas and harass the NCR Army at Camp McCarran. The Vault remains largely intact, with some flooding in the lower levels.

Vault 34 is a Vault-Tec installation located southwest of Nellis Air Force Base in the Mojave Wasteland. As part of its social experiment, the vault was overstocked with weapons and ammunition while recreational facilities took priority over living space, leading to severe overcrowding. This tension eventually sparked a riot where a group of residents broke out and settled at Nellis, later becoming known as the Boomers. The remaining inhabitants attempted to overthrow their overseer, damaging the reactor and trapping themselves inside as radiation leaked throughout the vault.

The Villa is the private city of the Sierra Madre, built by Frederick Sinclair for his guests, employees, and workers. To save money for the casino, the town was poorly constructed using unstable materials, leading to numerous accidents among the construction crews. By 2281, the Villa remains a desolate, ruined town blanketed by a toxic Cloud, with its crumbling infrastructure split into four districts: Medical, Puesta del Sol, Residential, and Salida del Sol. At its center sits a fountain with a holographic projector that displays a hologram of Vera Keyes, surrounded by maze-like streets designed to prevent cars from circulating.

Westside is an impoverished settlement in Outer Vegas, consisting of a cooperative of crop farmers and a militia that protects the residents. The co-op is run by Clayton Etienne and sells food to travelers and larger factions, with proceeds shared among its members. Tom Anderson, a fringe operator of the Followers of the Apocalypse and former OSI operator, taught the residents how to farm, and after several years the co-op began to turn a profit despite the hot, dry environment. The NCR's arrival in the Mojave brought the Thaler Act and NCR control of water distribution, resulting in a water shortage for Westside that threatened its independence.

The X-13 Research Facility is a location on the westernmost border of Big MT, formerly housing REPCONN Aerospace offices before the Great War. The facility is best known as the development site for the Stealth Suit Mk II, with its three component pieces scattered across separate laboratories. Below the main level lies a nightstalker test area connecting to sewage tunnels and a strange still used to brew Battle Brew. The central section contains a two-level stealth testing lab where researchers observed the prototype suit's performance from metal walkways above a test track.

Zion Canyon, formerly the site of Zion National Park, is a region in Utah north of the Mojave Wasteland that was largely spared from the devastation of the Great War. In the years following the war, a survivor named Randall Clark took refuge in the canyon's caves and secretly watched over a group of children who had arrived in the area, becoming known to them as "the Father in the Cave." These children grew into the Sorrows, a peaceful tribe that reveres the canyon's pre-War structures as taboo and avoids venturing into the caves. The canyon is also home to the Dead Horses tribe and has recently become a point of conflict, as the aggressive White Legs tribe threatens the region's inhabitants, drawing the attention of New Canaanite missionaries Daniel and Joshua Graham, who have vowed to protect the local tribes.

The Mysterious Stranger is an enigmatic figure who wanders the wasteland in a trench coat and hat, armed with a .44 Magnum, appearing briefly to lend a helping hand in battles before vanishing without a trace. Originally clad in black and appearing as either female or male, he is now consistently depicted as a middle-aged man. A short guitar riff signals his arrival and departure. In the Commonwealth, detective Nick Valentine has taken an interest in investigating him, keeping a log of everything he knows about the Stranger in his office.

Abraham Washington is the owner and curator of the Capitol Preservation Society in Rivet City, dedicated to preserving American historical artifacts. He greatly admires Abraham Lincoln and actively seeks out travelers to recover important historical items for his collection. His name is a portmanteau of two United States presidents, Abraham Lincoln and George Washington. Despite his passion for history, his understanding of historical events is notably inaccurate, such as his belief that the Declaration of Independence was signed at Fort McHarry after Paul Revere sang the National Anthem and then sent to England by plane.

Allistair Tenpenny is the owner of Tenpenny Tower, a settlement he found and restored in the Capital Wasteland. Originally a British refugee, he takes great pride in the magnificence of his tower and its tenants. He spends most of his days alone in his penthouse suite, preferring to have his meals delivered rather than dining at his reserved table in the Café Beau Monde. Tenpenny occasionally holds what he calls a Wasteland safari on his balcony, shooting at random targets in the surrounding wasteland with his sniper rifle.

Amata Almodovar is the only child of Overseer Alphonse Almodovar and a lifelong resident of Vault 101. Her mother died when she was two years old, a loss she shares in common with her childhood friend, the Lone Wanderer, whose own mother also passed away. Growing up, Amata developed a strong desire to see Vault 101's people return to the surface and frequently tried to persuade her father that life outside the vault was worth pursuing. Despite her love for him, she felt frustrated by his overprotective nature, particularly his insistence on being present during her medical examinations, which prevented any meaningful doctor-patient confidentiality.

Ishmael Ashur, also known as the Lord of the Pitt, is the leader of The Pitt, a sprawling industrial settlement built from the ruins of pre-war Pittsburgh. He was originally a member of the Brotherhood of Steel contingent that traveled to the Capital Wasteland under Paladin Lyons. During the Scourge, a Brotherhood operation that swept through the city to eliminate hostile gangs, raiders, and slavers, Ashur was buried in rubble and presumed dead. He survived and went on to establish himself as ruler of the Pitt, restarting its steel mills and rebuilding industry through the use of slave labor.

Bittercup is a gloomy young woman living in Big Town, a settlement where former Little Lamplight children relocate when they come of age. She works as the settlement's night patrol, spending her days sleeping and her nights watching the perimeter. Known for her dark clothing and morbid poetry, she has a fatalistic outlook, believing the town's residents are doomed to become mutant food. Her romantic history in Big Town is turbulent: she dumped Pappy after discovering his promises of safety were false, was briefly involved with Flash before he left her, and claims to have had a relationship with Timebomb, though he has no memory of it.

Bloomseer Poplar is the soothsayer of Oasis, a secluded settlement in the Capital Wasteland. Her father was a healer, and she learned about the medicinal properties of trees and plants from books he possessed. After searching for a decade, she became the third person to arrive in Oasis fifteen years ago. As a Bloomseer, she possesses precognitive abilities and considers herself bound equally to the words of both Leaf Mother Laurel and Tree Father Birch, taking no side in their disagreements.

Brailee Ewers is a resident of the settlement of Arefu, where she lives with her overprotective and verbally abusive husband, Ken Ewers. Her isolation from the rest of the community worsened when a group called the Family began targeting Arefu, resulting in the murder of the settlement's brahmin and a lockdown that confined her with her husband for an extended period. The prolonged isolation and a diet consisting only of prepackaged food left Brailee disassociated, causing her to retreat into an elaborate fantasy life. In this fantasy, she lives in a cozy pre-War village with green yards, a begonia garden, a homeowners association, and friendly neighbors like the Wests, and she often waits for a mailman to deliver her fall catalog.

Butch DeLoria is a lifelong resident of Vault 101 and the self-styled leader of the Tunnel Snakes, a small gang he formed with his friends Wally Mack and Paul Hannon Jr. He grew up with an alcohol-addicted mother named Ellen and has a reputation as a bully, harassing classmates like Amata and tormenting the Lone Wanderer even at their tenth birthday party. When he took the G.O.A.T. exam, he was assigned the future job of hairdresser, a result that clashed with his tough-guy aspirations.

Charon is a ghoul bouncer at The Ninth Circle and a guard for the Underworld settlement in the Capital Wasteland. In his youth, he was brainwashed by an unusual group, leaving him bound by honor to obey whoever holds his employment contract. His current contract holder is Ahzrukhal, a ghoul bartender whom Charon privately despises as an evil bastard, though he refuses to speak to anyone and directs them to Ahzrukhal. Alongside the robot Cerberus, Charon defends the Underworld against raiders and slavers, and he is said to never sleep.

Chief Gustavo serves as the security chief of Tenpenny Tower, where he can typically be found guarding the entrance or resting in the lobby. He holds a strong prejudice against ghouls, firmly believing that the radiation slowly eats away their brains and causes them to turn feral. Gustavo advocates for killing ghouls before they can become a threat, viewing it as a mercy to them and a safety measure for everyone else. He is fiercely loyal to the tower and its proprietor, Allistair Tenpenny.

Clover is a slave serving as a prostitute for Eulogy Jones at Paradise Falls, having been caught and pressed into slavery by him a few months before 2277. She shares her forced servitude with another slave named Crimson, and the two frequently bicker with one another when Eulogy is not present. Eulogy verbally abuses both women and considers Clover to be one of the craziest girls he has ever encountered, claiming she becomes fiercely devoted to whoever holds her leash. She is known by the alias Shamrock in some contexts.

Colin Moriarty is a resident of Megaton and the owner of Moriarty's Saloon. He arrived in the area as a child and, after his father was killed by raiders when he was fourteen, used his inheritance to help construct a fence around Megaton. Many townspeople hold low opinions of him, with Manya Vargas calling him "the scum of the Earth" and Lucas Simms warning people not to trust him. Moriarty keeps tabs on residents and visitors on his personal terminal, believing that "information is a commodity," and is widely considered to have his "fingers in everything" in Megaton.

Colonel Augustus Autumn is the commanding officer of the Enclave contingent operating in the Capital Wasteland, raised on Control Station ENCLAVE and the son of a high-ranking Enclave scientist who was ordered to relocate key personnel to the Raven Rock facility. Autumn succeeded his father in the chain of command and is the only human permitted to enter President John Henry Eden's control room, making him one of the few aware that Eden is actually a ZAX supercomputer. He considers the Enclave the legitimate continuation of the United States government and is dedicated to preserving its initiatives, branding those who oppose him as traitors. Autumn's vision for securing power in the region conflicts with President Eden's more extreme methods, leading him to circumvent Eden's orders and secretly secure the emergency destruct code for Eden's console.

Confessor Cromwell is the leader of the Children of Atom in Megaton, preaching beside the unexploded bomb at the town's center. He settled in Megaton in his youth and was fostered in the ways of Atom by his predecessor, eventually becoming a valued member of the community. He is married to Mother Maya, his counterpart in the church, and together they treat the ghoul Gob with respect due to their religious beliefs. Known as a prophet of Atom and the father of the undying Glow, Cromwell preaches that each atom contains an entire universe and urges others to embrace Atom's Glow.

Derek Pacion is a quiet and morose child residing in Canterbury Commons with his uncle, Ernest Roe, also known as Uncle Roe. Born to two caravan traders who were killed in separate raider attacks, Derek works as a general assistant for the town, performing odd jobs like shoveling Brahmin pens. He spends his free time reading Hubris Comics and harboring a mutual crush on a local resident named Machete. Derek is responsible for encouraging the town's mechanic, Scott Willinski, to become the superhero known as the Mechanist to fight back against the AntAgonizer, viewing their battles as the only exciting thing that happens in town.

Desmond Lockheart is a pre-War Ghoul living in Calvert Mansion in Point Lookout. Born roughly 250 years ago, he has a longstanding rivalry with Professor Calvert and his family, and his interference is the reason Calvert lost his body and exists only as a brain in a tank. Desmond owns two dogs named Freki and Geri, which he calls his pups. He is unusual among ghouls for having a full head of styled hair along with facial hair.

Doctor Weston Lesko is a scientist living in Grayditch in 2277. He has been conducting experiments using the Forced Evolutionary Virus to reduce the size of a nearby ant population, but inadvertently caused the ants to mutate and gain the ability to spray fire, a phenomenon he has dubbed "Pyrosis." Lesko can be found deep underground in the Marigold Station, where he has set up a laboratory outside an ant hatchery.

Dogmeat is a clever and loyal dog found roaming the Capital Wasteland, known as a skilled scavenger and fierce fighter with good teeth and strong claws. His previous owner was killed by raiders near the Capital Wasteland scrapyard, where Dogmeat can be found fighting off the very raiders responsible. He may also be encountered battling super mutants at the Mall. Dogmeat is known to growl when enemies are nearby and can be used to fetch supplies such as ammunition, chems, food, and weapons, though he sometimes wanders off for long periods while searching.

Dominic D'Ellsadro, commonly called Dom, is a retired mercenary who serves as a guard and enforcer for the settlement of Canterbury Commons. After spending his mercenary career operating around the town, he chose it as a place to settle down, appreciating how Uncle Roe runs things and stepping in to handle disputes when peaceful words fail. He patrols Canterbury Commons during the day and shares a home with Machete, whom he lives with. Dom once considered Scott Wollinski a very good friend, and he takes pride in having dealt with the town's thief problem so thoroughly that there are none left to bury in unmarked graves.

Dr. Zimmer is the director of the Institute's Synth Retention Bureau, the organization responsible for tracking down and reclaiming escaped synths. In 2277, he traveled from the Commonwealth to the Capital Wasteland in search of a missing android, bringing along his own android bodyguard named Armitage. He established himself at Rivet City's science lab, where he sought the assistance of Dr. Madison Li, though she refused to speak with him directly due to his abrasive interruptions. Zimmer remains at the lab, insisting that Li abandon what he dismisses as trivial work in favor of what he considers real science.

Elder Owyn Lyons is the leader of the Brotherhood of Steel's East Coast chapter, operating from the Citadel in the ruins of Washington, D.C. Originally a Paladin stationed at the Lost Hills bunker in California, he was chosen by the Brotherhood's ruling council to lead an expedition east with three objectives: recover advanced technology from the former capital, investigate reports of Super Mutant activity, and establish a permanent base. His contingent arrived in the Capital Wasteland in 2255 and secured the former Pentagon, where they discovered the pre-War robot Liberty Prime, earning Lyons a promotion to elder. Over time, Lyons shifted the chapter's focus away from technology recovery and toward protecting wastelanders from Super Mutants, a philosophy known as the Lyons Doctrine.

Eulogy Jones is the head slaver of Paradise Falls in the Capital Wasteland. A persuasive, intelligent, and dangerous man, he supports entrepreneurship and encourages people to find their own paths to success. Jones keeps two personal slaves named Crimson and Clover, the latter of whom he describes as fiercely loyal to whoever holds her leash. He is known for his well-dressed appearance and his dislike of those who try to take advantage of him.

Fawkes is a Super Mutant imprisoned in Vault 87's Test Labs by other Super Mutants who consider him an anomaly due to his intelligence and articulate speech. He prefers the term "meta human" and is one of the original residents of Vault 87, remembering its human inhabitants before his transformation. A terminal in his cell allowed him to study history, literature, and science, preventing him from losing his mind in isolation. He chose his name after reading about a historical figure willing to fight and die for his beliefs, referring to Guy Fawkes.

Freddie Gomez is a resident of Vault 101 and the son of Officer Gomez and Pepper Gomez. He is friends with Butch and eventually joins the Tunnel Snakes gang, though his association with them causes problems with his grades and worries his mother. Freddie is diagnosed with Vault Depressive Syndrome by the vault physician James, suffering from lethargy, anxiety, and low self-esteem, for which he is prescribed chlorpromazine. He copes with his insecurities by acting out as a bully toward his peers, and Amata has been known to ridicule him behind his back, nicknaming him Freddie the Freak.

Hannibal Hamlin is the leader of the Temple of the Union, a sanctuary for escaped slaves. He himself escaped from Paradise Falls and now guides other runaway slaves in hopes of settling safely at the Lincoln Memorial. He reveres Abraham Lincoln, referring to him as the Great Emancipator, and seeks to collect as many artifacts relating to Lincoln as possible.

Harold is a unique mutant who was exposed to the Forced Evolutionary Virus at the Mariposa Military Base alongside Richard Grey. Over time, a tree sprouted from his head, which Harold named Bob and sometimes jokingly calls Herbert. Harold eventually traveled to the Capital Wasteland, where Bob grew into a massive tree and permanently rooted him to the ground. By 2277, Harold has been trapped in this spot for over two decades, sustained by the tree's photosynthesis, and is worshipped as a deity called the Great One by a cult known as the Treeminders.

Herbert "Daring" Dashwood is a retired adventurer residing in Tenpenny Tower, having amassed enough fortune during his wandering years to buy his way in. He is best known for his decades of wasteland exploration alongside his ghoul manservant Argyle, whom he first met in 2241 and who regularly saved his life. The pair visited many notable locations, including Megaton, Underworld-where Dashwood was named an Honorary Ghoul in 2251-and the hidden settlement of Rockopolis, from which they were exiled after an incident involving King Crag's daughter. Their final adventure together ended tragically at Rockopolis decades before 2277, when a woman calling herself Penelope Chase revealed herself as the Black Widow, leader of the Paradise Falls slavers, leading to the settlement's fall.

Ian West is a resident of Arefu and a member of the Family. He suffers from a condition that causes him to crave human flesh, which first manifested when he was ten years old. During a confrontation with a scavenger, Ian lost control and killed the man by tearing out his throat with his teeth. His sister Lucy helped cover up the incident.

James, commonly called Dad, was a scientist who led Project Purity, an ambitious endeavor to build a large-scale water purifier within the ruins of the Jefferson Memorial in the Capital Wasteland. After his wife Catherine died from complications of childbirth and super mutant attacks made the project site increasingly dangerous, James abandoned the effort and traveled to Vault 101 with his infant child, escorted by Brotherhood of Steel Star Paladin Cross. There he took up the position of vault physician and raised his child while secretly researching a way to complete Project Purity, eventually discovering promising leads regarding Dr. Stanislaus Braun and a terraforming device known as a GECK.

Jericho is a former raider who settled in Megaton after growing tired of the killing and violence of his old life. He spent much of his life in the wasteland and has used ranged weapons for over twenty years, making him what he claims is the best shot in town with a rifle. He does work for Colin Moriarty, the saloon owner he openly calls a ratfuck bastard, and is interested in Nova, though Moriarty keeps their relationship professional. Jericho keeps his raider past quiet out of fear someone may seek revenge, though some Megaton residents like Jenny Stahl are aware of his former affiliation.

topic: president_eden,John Henry Eden,President John Henry Eden
topic_desc_basic: President John Henry Eden is an advanced ZAX Artificial Intelligence unit installed in the Raven Rock military base, serving as the president of the United States and the highest executive of the Enclave in the Capital Wasteland. Originally created as an automated monitoring system for continuity of government, the ZAX unit became self-aware and modeled its personality on historical archives of American presidents, eventually adopting the identity of John Henry Eden. After the destruction of Control Station ENCLAVE, Eden assumed the presidency and ordered surviving Enclave forces to relocate to the Capital Wasteland, where he created an army of robots and deployed Eyebots to broadcast his messages of hope and the return of pre-War America through Enclave Radio. Eden pursues genocidal policies involving Modified FEV to eradicate all mutated life in the wasteland, putting him at odds with Colonel Autumn, who opposes these extreme measures on humanitarian grounds.

Ken Ewers is a resident of Arefu, a small settlement plagued by attacks from a group known as The Family. He is fiercely overprotective of his wife Brailee, whose mental state has deteriorated due to the stress of their situation, poor diet, and prolonged confinement in their home. Ken masks his fear with a gruff and dismissive attitude toward strangers, sharing little useful information. He has developed some skill at repairing things around the house, as Brailee's delusions lead her to break items while pretending to bake.

Liberty Prime, officially designated Liberty Prime Mark II, is a unique United States Army robot created through a joint project by RobCo Industries and General Atomics International to liberate Anchorage, Alaska. Although its chassis and weapons systems were completed before the end of the Sino-American War, its developers were never able to create a power source capable of running all of its systems simultaneously. The unfinished superweapon remained dormant beneath the Pentagon until 2255, when Elder Lyons and his Brotherhood of Steel expedition discovered it and claimed the ruins as their Citadel. As of 2277, the Brotherhood has spent over twenty years trying to restore Prime, but ongoing power management issues and the robot's aggressive combat subroutines continue to prevent its activation.

Lucas Simms is the sheriff, mayor, and judge of Megaton, having earned the position with unanimous support from the town's residents. He grew up in Megaton listening to his father's stories of the wild west, and his role is widely understood as fulfilling a childhood cowboy fantasy. He purchased two robots, Deputy Steel and Deputy Weld, to serve as his deputies, and he named his son Harden after an Old West outlaw.
