Simms is also a member of the Regulators and defends Megaton from raider attacks alongside the town militia, once killing a raider leader named Boppo.

Lydia Montenegro is a resident of Tenpenny Tower and the owner of the Boutique Le Chic, which she considers her pride and joy. She is close friends with Michael Hawthorne, with whom she spends evenings drinking in the Federalist Lounge, and is also friendly with Tiffany Cheng, offering her advice on relationship problems. Montenegro maintains a playful rivalry with Anthony Ling, the owner of New Urban Apparel, and the two are often seen trading teasing remarks. She opposes the idea of ghouls moving into Tenpenny Tower, believing they would bring filth and even speaking approvingly of the possibility that they might be killed by security.

Doctor Madison Li, often referred to as Dr. Li, is a scientist residing in Rivet City where she conducts research on portable fusion power and hydroponics. She previously worked alongside James and Catherine on Project Purity, an ambitious endeavor to cleanse the Tidal Basin of contaminants using the Jefferson Memorial. Her science team eventually took over the Rivet City Science Lab and Horace Pinkerton's seat on the city council to assist with the project.

Manya is a long-time resident of Megaton and the wife of Nathan, whom she met while working caravan routes with her father. Together, she and Nathan ran their own caravan line for over thirty years before saving enough caps to retire in Megaton. Her grandfather was one of the original settlers of the town, and her father helped build Megaton's walls using metal from deconstructed planes, making her knowledgeable about the town's history. Manya has lived in Megaton longer than anyone else, and settlers often say she can be asked just about anything about the town and its residents.

Mister Burke is the personal assistant of Allistair Tenpenny, the wealthy proprietor of Tenpenny Tower. He entered Tenpenny's service within the last twenty years and has since lived a considerably easier life. Burke can typically be found staying at Moriarty's Saloon in the settlement of Megaton, though he also maintains a house in town. After Tenpenny complained about the sight of Megaton marring the horizon from his tower, Burke offered to handle the situation personally.

Moira Brown is the owner of Megaton's Craterside Supply, where she lives upstairs and spends her days trading, sweeping, and conducting experiments. Originally from Canterbury Commons, she has lived in Megaton for at least ten to twelve years. Although she is highly intelligent, she lacks actual experience in the wasteland. Following a recent incident with a domesticated Centaur, she has decided to write a survival guide.

Nova is a resident of Megaton who works as a prostitute at Moriarty's Saloon, where she spends most of her time socializing with Gob, Colin Moriarty, Jericho, and other patrons. She has lived in Megaton for five years but has grown disillusioned, largely because Moriarty confiscates her earnings and locks them up for himself. Nova also has a Jet habit that displeases Moriarty, and she keeps out of other people's business to survive, never publicly acting against his interests. She refuses to serve ghouls despite her otherwise low standards, and she appears interested in Jericho but declines his advances because Moriarty disapproves of her dating non-customers.

Old Man Harris is an elderly resident of Andale who lives alone in a small shack on the edge of town. Since the death of his wife Gladys, he rarely leaves his home and relies on other residents to bring him meals. He had one daughter, Linda, who married Jack Smith, and he is also referred to as father by Martha Wilson. Harris is deeply disturbed by the true nature of Andale's inhabitants and warns visitors that the town's friendly appearance is a trick, urging them to leave immediately.

Paladin Kodiak, born Greg Bear, is a member of the Lyons' Pride and the last living survivor of the children brought from the Pitt to the Citadel by Elder Lyons during the Scourge. He grew up in the Pitt alongside his two older brothers, John and Grudd, never knowing his parents, but his brothers were left behind during the Scourge for being considered too savage. Kodiak became the largest and strongest member of the Lyons' Pride, excelling in close quarters combat with a Super Sledge and considering himself a jack of all trades skilled in recon, demolition, and tactical assault. He holds deep reverence for Elder Lyons, viewing him as a father figure, and can typically be found around the great hall in the A ring area of the Citadel.

Dr. Horace Pinkerton, often known simply as Pinkerton, is a reclusive scientist and surgeon living in the broken bow of Rivet City. He helped found Rivet City decades ago after clearing Mirelurks from an abandoned aircraft carrier and establishing a science lab, later forming the settlement's first council. After Doctor Li arrived and drew his science team toward Project Purity, Pinkerton was forced off the council and retreated into self-imposed exile in the ship's broken bow, where most Rivet City residents now consider him a legend.

Pronto is the sole proprietor of Lock and Load, a weapons shop located in Paradise Falls. He took over the business after the previous owner died and is rumored to be the son of an old slaver, though the slavers give him little respect. Most of his stock comes from slavers who loot weapons from guards, wastelanders, and captured slaves, though they keep the better weapons for themselves, leaving Pronto with a poor selection. He supplements his inventory by disassembling and reassembling weapons himself and occasionally designing his own.

Protector Henry Casdin is the leader of the Brotherhood of Steel Outcasts, a faction that broke away from Elder Lyons' chapter in the Capital Wasteland. Casdin was once one of Lyons' most accomplished soldiers and fought alongside him during the Scourge of the Pitt, but he and others came to view Lyons' focus on fighting super mutants and protecting local communities as a betrayal of the Brotherhood's core mission of technology retrieval. The dissenters rallied behind Casdin, abandoned the Citadel, and took a large portion of weapons and equipment with them, significantly weakening Lyons' chapter. They seized Fort Independence, a pre-War military base, drove out the raiders there, and established it as their headquarters.

Reilly is the leader of Reilly's Rangers, a small mercenary band dedicated to mapping the Capital Wasteland. Raised in Washington, D.C. by a military man who taught her self-sufficiency, she carried her adoptive father to Arlington National Cemetery for a proper burial after his death. At age 26 she founded the Rangers and has worked with her team for years, trusting each member with her life.

Ronald Laren is one of only two inhabitants of Girdershade, having settled there after his wife's death. He stays because of Sierra Petrovita, whom he considers his woman and hopes to sleep with. To win her favor, he gifted her a Vending Machine and ordered a special outfit from Grady over a year ago. He is a skilled fighter, having killed two Raiders at Girdershade and punched Lug-Nut.

Scribe Elizabeth Jameson serves as the Proctor for the Order of the Quill and the Keeper of the Scrolls for the East Coast Brotherhood of Steel, operating out of the Citadel. She is charged with protecting and maintaining technical manuals and the records of deeds for all members of the East Coast chapter. Due to the chapter's lack of communication equipment and manpower, many deaths in the field go unreported, leaving her unable to properly record the fates of missing patrols and fallen brethren in the scrolls. As a scribe, she studies, compiles, and utilizes the knowledge the Brotherhood discovers, and is a student of their history.

Scribe Rothchild oversees the scribes of the Brotherhood of Steel in the Capital Wasteland and is a leading scientific mind in fields such as robotics and cybernetics. He joined Owyn Lyons' expedition to Washington, D.C. in 2255 and was tasked with bringing the massive Liberty Prime weapon online. Though personally loyal to Elder Lyons, Rothchild openly criticized the elder's insubordination against the western elders, which led to the Outcasts' departure in 2276 and the chapter being cut off from reinforcements. He collaborated with outside scientists including James of Project Purity and later Madison Li, whose expertise helped provide enough power for Liberty Prime's systems.

Seagrave Holmes is a merchant operating a junk shop in Rivet City. He formerly sold captured Wastelanders to his friend Eulogy Jones of Paradise Falls, but has since abandoned that business and ignores Jones's attempts to lure him back. Holmes suffers from a chronic respiratory disease called Red-Lung, caused by his repair work below the carrier's decks. He is romantically interested in Vera Weatherly, who manages the Weatherly Hotel, but she considers him only a friend and wishes to keep their relationship platonic.

Sentinel Sarah Lyons is the commander of the Lyons' Pride, an elite Brotherhood of Steel squad operating in the ruins of Washington, D.C. Born at the Brotherhood's West Coast headquarters, she accompanied her father Elder Owyn Lyons on his expedition east after her mother's death. She is widely regarded as one of the Brotherhood's finest warriors and personally selects who joins her squad. At the Citadel, she serves as a mentor and role model for young Squire Arthur Maxson, who has learned combat skills from her and holds her in high regard.

Sergeant RL-3 is a customized Mister Gutsy model created by General Atomics for mobile attacks before the Great War. A wandering trader named Tinker Joe scavenged the robot from parts and now offers it for sale while traveling between the RobCo Facility and Tenpenny Tower. RL-3 possesses a simulated personality unit, but due to programming issues it is picky about the company it keeps, refusing to travel with anyone it considers too extreme. This stubborn selectivity has made it difficult for Tinker Joe to sell the robot.

Arthur Maxson, commonly called Squire Maxson, is the last known descendant of Roger Maxson, the founder of the Brotherhood of Steel. Born in 2267 to Lady Jessica Maxson and the paladin Jonathan, he was sent east as an infant to be raised by Elder Owyn Lyons at the Citadel. A studious boy, he learned Brotherhood history and combat from Sentinel Sarah Lyons, though he was barred from patrols after accidentally shooting her. He dreams of befriending Liberty Prime and sneaks into Paladin Vargas's room to read Guns and Bullets.

Star Paladin Cross is the Seneschal of Elder Lyons and the highest ranking soldier in the Brotherhood of Steel's East Coast chapter, answering only to Elder Lyons himself. She also holds the title of Keeper of the ARM. During a field mission protecting Elder Lyons, Cross was critically injured and saved through cybernetic augmentation performed by Scribe Rothchild, leaving her with no need for food or sleep. She was responsible for defending Project Purity against Super Mutant attacks during its early stages, and she later escorted James and his newborn child to Megaton after the death of Catherine.

Sticky, also known as "Sticky Hands" and sometimes calling himself "Jack," is a resident of Little Lamplight who recently turned sixteen. By the settlement's custom, children who come of age must leave the relative safety of Little Lamplight and relocate to Big Town. Sticky is unhappy about being forced out and frequently complains about the rules while trying to bend them in his favor. On the bright side, his girlfriend Red already lives in Big Town, giving him at least one reason to look forward to the move.

Synths, also called androids, are bio-synthetic beings manufactured by the Institute in the Commonwealth. They range in appearance from clearly robotic to virtually indistinguishable from a human, and are used by the Institute for maintenance, labor, combat, requisitions, and experimentation. Each Synth is issued a designation number for identification, such as A3-21 or S3-47. By 2277, Synths had appeared in the Capital Wasteland, where at least one advanced model was known to be hiding among the population.

The AntAgonizer, born Tanya Christoff, is a self-proclaimed supervillain in Canterbury Commons who commands giant ants and battles the Mechanist. Inspired by a Grognak comic, she believes humanity is doomed due to past mistreatment and prefers the company of ants. Her rivalry with the Mechanist began when she destroyed his female robot, and she offers rewards for his defeat.

Three Dog is the host of Galaxy News Radio, broadcasting from the GNR Building Plaza in the Capital Wasteland with the protection of the Brotherhood of Steel. Born to parents in a traveling theatre group, he was raised on rock music and the ideals of free speech, learning to distinguish propaganda from truth. He fights what he calls the Good Fight, using his broadcasts to report the harsh realities of the wasteland and to counteract the propaganda of the Enclave and their radio station. His engineer assistant Margaret helps keep the station operational, and together they warn wasteland residents of threats from slavers, raiders, and super mutants.

Tree Father Birch is the leader of the Treeminders, a group residing in the secluded settlement of Oasis. He founded the Treeminders to protect the being they revere as the One Who Grows, the One Who Gives, and the One Who Guides, whose name is never spoken out of reverence. Leaf Mother Laurel joined him a year after the group's founding, followed by Bloomseer Poplar, whom Birch initially distrusted but accepted at Laurel's urging. Together the three developed the Ceremony of Purification.

Wally Mack is a resident of Vault 101 and a member of the Tunnel Snakes, a small gang of youths who harass other students in the vault. He is the son of Allen and Gloria Mack and the brother of Susie and Stevie Mack. His friends and fellow gang members include Butch DeLoria and Paul Hannon Jr. Though Butch presumes to lead the Tunnel Snakes, Wally might disagree if challenged on the matter.

Wernher is an escaped slave and former right-hand man of Ishmael Ashur in The Pitt. He is organizing a slave revolt against Ashur in collaboration with Midea. To enact his plan, he requires the assistance of an outsider to infiltrate the Pitt raiders without being recognized. He broadcasted a radio distress call to alert anyone who would listen to his situation.

Aaron Kimball is the president of the New California Republic, often called the Hero of the Mojave for his 2270 military campaign against tribals threatening NCR citizens. After retiring from the military in 2273, he entered politics with Ambassador Dennis Crocker's help, winning a council seat and soon replacing Wendell Peterson as president. His first act was ordering the occupation of Hoover Dam, whose water and electricity boosted his popularity. He overturned President Tandi's limits on animal and acreage ownership, benefiting groups like the Stockmen's Association.

Dennis Crocker is the New California Republic's ambassador to New Vegas, formally titled "Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary" of the Department of State. He began his political career as a mayor twenty years ago and rose through the ranks, eventually heading President Kimball's successful campaign for NCR council. Crocker is the third person to hold the ambassadorship, following Susanna Edith and Phillip Granger, and is in his seventh year in the role. He focuses on day-to-day paperwork and helping NCR police keep troops in line on the Strip, accepting the limits of his position rather than pursuing annexation of the Mojave.

Antony, sometimes spelled Anthony, serves as the Master of the Hounds for Caesar's Legion at the Fort. He was born among the Hangdogs, a tribe on the outskirts of Denver, Colorado, where he spent his life training dogs and revering them as the tribe's spirit animals. When Caesar's Legion arrived, the Hangdogs resisted longer than most tribes until Legate Lanius broke them by burning their dogs, after which the tribe was conscripted as houndmasters. Antony now breeds dogs for the Legion, including Lupa, the fiercest hound in their ranks.

Benny is the head of the Chairmen, a tribe that operates The Tops casino on the New Vegas Strip. Originally a member of the Mojave Boot-Riders, he killed the tribe's chief, Bingo, in a knife fight to take leadership and accept Mr. House's offer to transform the tribe into a casino-running family. Benny's long-term ambition is to seize control of New Vegas for himself.

Caesar, born Edward Sallow in 2226, is the ruler and co-founder of Caesar's Legion. Raised by the Followers of the Apocalypse in the Boneyard, he became an anthropologist and linguist before being sent east to study the tribes of the Grand Canyon. After being captured by the Blackfoot tribe, he taught them Roman-style warfare from old books, leading them to conquer and assimilate neighboring tribes. He erased tribal identities, crowned himself Caesar, and formed the Legion, modeling it after Imperial Rome.

Captain Ronald Curtis, known to Caesar's Legion by the codename Picus, is a frumentarius who spent years infiltrating the New California Republic Army and rose to the rank of captain in just over three years. He commands Bravo Company at Camp McCarran, where General Lee Oliver placed his unit to bolster the base's defenses, and he assists Colonel James Hsu with logistics. Using his trusted position, Picus discreetly feeds the Legion intelligence on NCR patrols and plans while working toward a major sabotage operation targeting the McCarran-Vegas monorail. He maintains an informant named Martina Groesbeck on the New Vegas Strip and is monitored closely by Vulpes Inculta, the leader of the Legion's frumentarii.

Rose of Sharon Cassidy, commonly known as Cass or Whiskey Rose, is the owner of Cassidy Caravans, a merchant company operating in the Mojave Wasteland. She was raised by her mother, a former tribal from east of the Colorado River, after her father left to wander the wastes when she was still young, leaving her only a name and a pendant. Cass inherited her father's heart problems along with his name, and has spent years running caravans across the harsh desert roads. She is known for her hard-drinking lifestyle and outspoken opinions on both the NCR's bureaucratic inefficiency and Caesar's Legion's brutal treatment of women, though she concedes that Legion supply lines are remarkably safe compared to those of the NCR.

Chief Hanlon is the grizzled leader of the NCR Rangers, stationed at Camp Golf in the Mojave Wasteland. A veteran of over 40 years, he coordinated Ranger operations and became a war hero after his strategy at the First Battle of Hoover Dam broke the Legion's offensive by luring their forces into Boulder City and blowing it up. Despite his legendary reputation for misdirection and ambushes, Hanlon grew disillusioned with the NCR's expansionist ambitions, believing that holding the Dam and New Vegas would eventually destroy the Republic. He secretly sabotaged the war effort by falsifying intelligence reports from Ranger stations across the Mojave, hoping to convince NCR leadership to abandon the frontier.

Chris Haversam is an engineer living at the REPCONN Test Site who believes himself to be a ghoul. He grew up in Vault 34, where he was assigned as the vault reactor engineer due to his technical aptitude and his preference for machines over weapons. He became convinced that radiation from the vault reactor was turning him into a ghoul, and when his hair began falling out for natural reasons, he left the vault. Shortly after his departure, the vault's reactor became unstable and actually irradiated most of the residents, turning them into ghouls.

Christine Royce is a former scribe of the Brotherhood of Steel and a knight of The Circle who was tasked with hunting down the rogue elder Father Elijah. While tracking him to the Big MT, she was captured and lobotomized, leaving her with deep facial scars and an impaired ability to read and write. After being rescued by a fellow traveler named Ulysses, she followed Elijah's trail to the Sierra Madre, where she was fitted with a slave collar and trapped inside an Auto-Doc by Dean Domino. During her imprisonment, Domino surgically removed her vocal cords in an attempt to replicate the voice of Vera Keyes for his vault heist.

topic: colonel_hsu,Col. James Hsu,Colonel James Hsu,James Hsu,Hsu
topic_desc_basic: Colonel James Hsu is the commanding officer of the New California Republic Army garrison at Camp McCarran and oversees most NCR military operations in the Mojave Wasteland. A level-headed and competent officer, he is known for favoring diplomacy over force of arms, caring deeply for the soldiers under his command, and being sympathetic to local populations, including his management of water and power distribution in Freeside. His modesty and competence have made him well-liked by his troops, though this has drawn the ire of General Lee Oliver, who views him as a potential rival. Hsu previously served alongside Nathan, the future warden of the NCR Correctional Facility, for seven years and still owed him a favor from an incident in Modoc.

Corporal Betsy is a sniper serving in Alpha Team of the New California Republic Army's First Recon, stationed at Camp McCarran under Lieutenant Gorobets. She works in a sniper pair with 10 of Spades, having volunteered to partner with him when no one else would due to his lack of experience, and she allows him to wear eyeglasses she calls his training shades to cover for his poor eyesight. Betsy struggles with anger and behavioral issues stemming from trauma after being sexually assaulted by the Fiend leader Cook-Cook, an incident that left her partner knocked unconscious and blaming himself. Her commanding officer recognizes her behavior is inappropriate but would prefer she seek treatment rather than face punishment, though Betsy is initially reluctant to acknowledge the experience has affected her or that seeing a doctor would help.

Corporal Sterling is a member of NCR First Recon's Alpha Team stationed at Camp McCarran and is one of the outfit's oldest members. Formerly an NCR Ranger, he was among the first to scout the Mojave Wasteland in 2273, walking vast stretches of territory between Shady Sands and the Colorado River and learning about local tribes to pave the way for the Mojave Campaign. His Ranger career ended after Legionaries captured him near Malpais and smashed the bones in his hands and feet, though he escaped by crawling to a cliff and tumbling into the Colorado, where fellow Rangers rescued him from drowning. Although the lasting damage prevented him from handling a sidearm or conducting long-range patrols, Sterling's persistence and marksmanship earned him a place in the Army, and Lieutenant Gorobets transferred him to First Recon.

Corporal William Farber serves as a mess officer for the NCR Army at Camp McCarran, where he is responsible for cooking, preparing, and serving meals to the troopers stationed there. His ability to produce quality food is hampered by a lack of meat and spices, leaving him limited to vegetables such as corn, beans, and onions, which affects both morale and digestion among the soldiers. The base's food processor is also in need of repair and replacement parts, further complicating his duties. Farber was once tricked by an NCR health inspector, from whom he bribed 50 caps, and the researcher Keely in Vault 22 suspects that a sample derived from the vault's spore plants might be of interest to him.

Craig Boone is a retired New California Republic First Recon sharpshooter who currently works as the night-shift town guard in Novac. During his military service, he fought in the First Battle of Hoover Dam and participated in the Bitter Springs Massacre, where he was ordered to fire on fleeing non-combatants. After leaving the army, he settled in Novac with his wife Carla and his former spotter Manny Vargas. Following Carla's kidnapping by Caesar's Legion, Boone tracked her to a Legion outpost and chose to mercy kill her rather than let her be enslaved, leaving him embittered and determined to find whoever was responsible for her abduction.

Daniel is a New Canaanite missionary operating among the Sorrows tribe in Zion Canyon. Originally dispatched by Bishop Mordecai to spread the word of God, Daniel's mission shifted after he witnessed the destruction of New Canaan and the death of his bishop. He now dedicates himself to protecting the Sorrows from the White Legs, a hostile tribe responsible for attacking New Canaan, and fears that war would corrupt their innocent nature. Daniel's teachings blended New Canaanite theology with the Sorrows' existing spiritual beliefs, causing their Father in the Cave and the New Canaanite God to become one and the same.

Dean Domino, also known as the King of Swing, was a famous pre-War lounge singer who performed across the United States and Europe, including the Las Vegas Strip. He was invited to perform at the Sierra Madre casino, where he became consumed with jealousy toward the casino's founder, Frederick Sinclair, and plotted to break into the vault using his former lover Vera Keyes. When the bombs dropped, the Gala Event became a massacre and Dean was trapped in the Sierra Madre, undergoing ghoulification over the next two hundred years while obsessively mapping the casino's security system and plotting his grand heist. He was eventually captured by Dog, fitted with an explosive collar, and forced to work for Father Elijah.

Deputy Beagle is the deputy of Primm, deputized by Sheriff McBain roughly two and a half months before the convict attack on the town, largely on account of being the sheriff's wife's brother. He is widely regarded by Primm's inhabitants as lacking in common sense, intelligence, and general usefulness, a reputation he attempts to offset with a gentlemanly demeanor and sophisticated vocabulary that he frequently mispronounces. Beagle is also known as a lazy coward who avoids proactive law enforcement and leaves tasks half-finished, having earned his position through family ties rather than merit. During the convict takeover of Primm, Beagle was taken hostage after witnessing the murder of Sheriff McBain and his own sister, and was tortured into revealing what little he knew about the town before being held for a ransom that no one in Primm could afford to pay.

Doc Mitchell is a surgeon and doctor living in Goodsprings. He grew up in Vault 21 beneath the New Vegas Strip, where younger residents gave him the nickname mole-butt. When Mr. House opened and filled Vault 21 with concrete during the Strip renovations beginning in 2274, Mitchell was forced into homelessness and worked as a traveling doctor, finding his medical expertise rare and valuable in the wasteland.

Doctor Henry is a physician and former Enclave scientist who eventually settled in Jacobstown within the Mojave Wasteland alongside other Enclave Remnants. During his time with the Enclave, he specialized in human and canine neuroscience and worked on canine cyber-genetics, though he left the organization after disagreeing with their initiative to simply kill super mutants instead of curing them. After departing before the destruction of the Enclave oil rig, he spent time in the New California Republic and traveling with caravans before relocating to Jacobstown. There, he established a lab in the lodge to research the effects of prolonged Stealth Boy Mark II Prototype usage by Nightkin, aiming to cure their schizophrenia.

Doctor Klein is a pre-War scientist and the Chief Head Researcher of Logistical Operations and Idea-ology at Big MT. After the Great War, he became a Think Tank, a disembodied brain housed in a robotic chassis, to continue his work alongside his colleagues. He serves as the leader of the Think Tank, acting with a stuffy, authoritative demeanor reminiscent of a college dean, and often refuses to confer with his peers on decisions. Despite his general hostility toward Doctor Mobius, he retains some willingness to consider him a partner under certain circumstances.

Doctor Mobius is a Think Tank operating in the Big MT and the leader of the Robo-Scorpion army. He is the nemesis of Dr. Klein and the team to which he belonged. Mobius was part of the Big MT Think Tank before the Great War and became a think tank after the War to continue his work.

Dog and God are two distinct identities sharing the body of a single Nightkin, a product of trauma-induced dissociative identity disorder. Dog, the childlike and perpetually hungry persona, served in the Master's army as a stealth trooper before following the Sierra Madre Broadcast to the Sierra Madre casino, where Father Elijah became his new master. God, the intelligent and controlling persona, acts as Dog's conscience, attempting to restrain his destructive instincts. The two identities take turns controlling their shared body, with the dormant one confined to a mental cage where they can hear but not witness outside events.

ED-E (Eyebot Duraframe Subject E, pronounced "Eddie" or "E-D-E") is a prototype duraframe eyebot manufactured by the Enclave for combat use, featuring enhancements over standard eyebots including additional sensor dishes, armor plating for side-mounted vacuum tubes, and a miniaturized Tesla cannon. When the Enclave halted duraframe production to focus on Hellfire armor and destroyed all remaining units, ED-E became the last surviving model. Dr. Whitley, the head researcher of the duraframe project, uploaded Poseidon Energy data and his research into ED-E's logs and dispatched it toward Navarro, but it stopped at an Enclave outpost in Chicago for repairs before crossing the Mojave Wasteland, where a raider sniper shot and damaged it.

Easy Pete is a former prospector living in Goodsprings who earned his nickname by "taking it easy" and helping tend to the town's brahmin and bighorners. Before settling down, he scoured old buildings for tech, weapons, chems, and spare parts, and once found a promising claim near the Colorado River before raiders chased him off. He is experienced with dynamite, which he keeps buried for safekeeping, and refuses to share it with anyone who doesn't know explosives. Pete is knowledgeable about the broader regional conflict, describing Caesar's Legion as slavers led by Caesar and noting that the NCR beat them back at the First Battle of Hoover Dam but failed to finish the job.

Elder Nolan McNamara is the leader of the Mojave Chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel, operating from the Hidden Valley Bunker. He earned the respect and loyalty of his chapter by breaking through NCR lines at HELIOS One during the failed Operation Sunburst, leading surviving Brotherhood forces to safety. When Father Elijah vanished during that battle, McNamara assumed command and the rank of elder, credited with saving the Mojave chapter from complete eradication. Fearing continued NCR pursuit, he placed the Hidden Valley bunker on lockdown, restricting movement to small scouting parties and barring entry to outside members, though the NCR is actually overburdened on multiple fronts and not actively hunting the Brotherhood.

Doctor Emily Ortal is a physician and member of the Followers of the Apocalypse who works in the Mojave Wasteland. She chose to operate there because neither the OSI nor other NCR-aligned organizations funded medical research unless it had military applications, and inflation and taxation in Republic territories further motivated her decision. She is responsible for reprogramming the Securitron known as Yes Man for Benny, modifying it to connect to the network so that Mr. House could not remotely disable it.

Fantastic is an incompetent and egotistical con artist employed by the NCR as a technician at HELIOS One, having talked his way into the job by claiming to have a "theoretical degree in physics." Since arriving, he has done virtually nothing to repair the plant, instead convincing NCR personnel that he is essential so he can keep drawing pay to fuel his drug addiction. He works alongside Ignacio Rivas, who is far more knowledgeable but whom Fantastic ignores, and he has spent months working on what is actually the intercom console while the plant runs at one percent efficiency. Most NCR soldiers and Rivas have little respect for him, and anyone who spends time around him quickly sees through his fraud.

Father Elijah is a former Elder of the Brotherhood of Steel, notable for being a Scribe promoted to a rank typically reserved for Paladins due to his exceptional aptitude for advanced technology. Unlike traditional Brotherhood leadership, Elijah emphasized the enhancement and development of pre-War technology rather than mere preservation, a philosophy that brought him into conflict with the organization's leadership and led to his reassignment to the Mojave region. There he redirected Brotherhood operations to HELIOS One, a solar energy facility, where he sought to activate the experimental ARCHIMEDES II weapon system to counter the New California Republic. When the NCR overran the facility during Operation: Sunburst, Elijah disappeared, abandoning the Brotherhood and its remaining forces.

General Lee Oliver is a career New California Republic Army soldier and an outspoken supporter of President Aaron Kimball who serves as the commander of the republic's forces in the Mojave Wasteland. He is responsible for the overall strategy of NCR forces in the region and is preparing for the Second Battle of Hoover Dam, where he intends to confront Caesar's Legion en masse and destroy the enemy through attrition. Many lower-ranking officers and soldiers hold a low opinion of him, believing he obtained his post largely through cronyism, and his cautious approach has earned him the defamatory moniker General Wait-and-see. Oliver holds a grudge against the NCR Rangers and Chief Hanlon over the role they played in the First Battle of Hoover Dam, and he is determined to win the second battle entirely through his own methods.

Gloria Van Graff, also known as Glory, is the manager of the Silver Rush energy weapons store in Freeside, a position she holds alongside her older brother Jean-Baptiste Cutting. The Van Graff family expanded from Redding into the Mojave Wasteland under their mother's direction, and Gloria is one of ten siblings who each run different branches. Despite her sharp intellect, she receives undesirable assignments because she and her mother do not get along. Gloria took over the Silver Rush after her sister Frieda left, and the Van Graffs seized the location by force, killing members of the Kings who resisted.

Head Paladin Hardin, also known as Edgar Hardin, is the head paladin of the Mojave chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel and its most experienced veteran. He was a key advisor to Father Elijah and attempted to convince the elder to abandon HELIOS One before the NCR overran the perimeter. After retreating to the Hidden Valley Bunker under acting elder Nolan McNamara, Hardin grew disillusioned with the ongoing lockdown and McNamara's refusal to send out scouts or patrols. Convinced that the chapter is stagnating and failing its mission, Hardin has considered ways to remove McNamara from leadership, restrained only by his respect for the elder's actions at HELIOS One.

Jas Wilkins is a food merchant and cook operating the Mess Hall at Sloan in the Mojave Wasteland. Originally from California, she traveled east because she found life under the NCR too safe and boring, drawn by the freedom of New Vegas. Her great-aunt Rose ran a Bed & Breakfast in Modoc and kept a female Deathclaw in a shed to harvest eggs for Deathclaw Omelets, a recipe passed down to Jas. The quarry workers at Sloan complain about her coffee.

Jeannie May Crawford is the owner-operator of the Dino Dee-lite Motel in the frontier town of Novac. She is a proud businesswoman who defends her town and its hardworking citizens against criticism. She fears the ghouls inhabiting the nearby REPCONN Test Site, believing they threaten the salvage-based economy that sustains Novac. Despite her welcoming demeanor, she is secretly responsible for selling Craig Boone's wife Carla into slavery to Caesar's Legion.

Jerry the Punk is a young Great Khan living at Red Rock Canyon who harbors an unusual passion for poetry, a talent he developed after reading Pre-War books provided to the tribe by the Followers of the Apocalypse. Though he considers the Great Khans his family, he feels out of place among them and has failed the tribe's initiation five times. His poems often blend romantic longing with the harsh realities of Khan life, including rejection by women and beatings at the hands of their brothers. Jerry dreams of leaving the canyon to join the Followers of the Apocalypse at the Old Mormon Fort in Freeside, where he hopes to find people who better appreciate his sensitive nature.

Joshua Graham, also known as the Malpais Legate and the Burned Man, is a New Canaanite missionary and former co-founder of Caesar's Legion. After helping Caesar forge his empire for thirty years, Graham led the failed assault on Hoover Dam in 2277, resulting in Caesar having him burned alive and cast into the Grand Canyon. He survived the execution attempt and returned to New Canaan, but a subsequent attack by the White Legs tribe destroyed the settlement and forced him to flee with survivors to Zion Canyon. There, he lives among the Sorrows tribe and prepares to make a stand against the pursuing White Legs, despite fellow New Canaanite Daniel advocating for evacuation.

Judah Kreger is a former Enclave captain living in the Westside community of the Mojave Wasteland. He served as an Enclave officer in command of a squad stationed at Navarro that included Cannibal Johnson, Orion Moreno, Daisy Whitman, Doctor Henry, and Arcade Gannon's father. Kreger's leadership kept Johnson and Moreno from tearing each other apart and served as the bond holding the group together. After the destruction of Control Station ENCLAVE and the NCR's sacking of Navarro, he fled alongside other Enclave survivors to avoid violence at the hands of the NCR and Brotherhood of Steel.

Klamath Bob, often simply called Bob, is a shopkeeper living in the Westside settlement of New Vegas. Originally from the northern town of Klamath, he recalls his hometown as a dull but pleasant place known for hunting, eating, and skinning geckos. He runs a liquor store named after himself, supplying residents who need a drink to face the day, and after hours he patrols Westside to help keep the peace despite his limited skill with firearms. Bob is also known for his friendship with Mean Sonofabitch, a Super Mutant veteran of the Unity, whom he once tried to protect from abuse in The Hub and who later followed him to Westside, where the mutant now performs odd jobs and helps defend the community.

topic: legate_lanius,Monster of the East,Terror of the East
topic_desc_basic: Legate Lanius, known as the Monster of the East or Terror of the East, serves as the military commander of Caesar's Legion, having replaced Joshua Graham in that role following the Legion's defeat at the First Battle of Hoover Dam. Originally the most formidable warrior of the Hidebarks, an Arizona tribe, Lanius turned on his own people after their chief surrendered to the Legion, slaughtering fifteen warriors before being subdued. Caesar granted him the name Lanius, meaning "butcher," and he pledged loyalty on the condition that he be allowed to execute all surviving males of his tribe. He is loyal only to Caesar himself, caring nothing for battlefield losses so long as the enemy suffers more, and Caesar relies on him to enforce brutal disciplinary measures against underperforming officers.

Lily is an elderly Nightkin residing in Jacobstown, a settlement led by the super mutant Marcus, where she tends to bighorners. Born a human in Vault 17, she was transformed into a Nightkin at age 75 by the Master and served as an assassin and spy in his army under squad leader Tabitha until the Cathedral's destruction, after which she attempted to return home. She carries a sword fashioned from a crashed vertibird blade near Klamath and keeps a holotape of her grandchildren, Becky and Jimmy, whose memories she fiercely protects. Lily suffers from schizophrenia caused by excessive Stealth Boy use, manifesting as a second personality named Leo, and receives treatment from Doctor Henry with antipsychotic drugs, though she resists full dosages due to the memory loss side effects.

Lieutenant Carrie Boyd is a military police officer stationed at Camp McCarran, where she serves as the officer in charge of policing duties for the base. She handles break-ins, thefts, investigations into missing soldiers, and the interrogation of prisoners. Boyd reports to Colonel Hsu and operates from her office on the east side of the second floor. Known for her sharp tongue and no-nonsense attitude, she has expressed a willingness to use harsher interrogation tactics than NCR regulations typically allow, noting that some restrictions on such methods date back to President Tandi's administration.

Major Knight is an NCR Army officer stationed at the Mojave Outpost, where he has spent a long time logging caravan traffic that keeps building up as more people arrive than leave. He is an expert repairman who fixes soldiers' and travelers' gear in exchange for caps, charging a hefty sum for his services. Although the Mojave Outpost serves as the administrative headquarters for the area around Primm, bureaucratic red tape prevents Knight from offering support to Lieutenant Hayes's unit stationed near Primm, a situation that frustrates him. Knight is homosexual but keeps his sexuality hidden while at the outpost, explaining that while such relationships are accepted back in California, they do not fare well on the fringes of the Republic, and he prefers to stay professional on duty rather than risk the disapproval of his fellow soldiers.

Old Ben is a lifelong resident of Freeside who worked at his father's butcher shop until a competitor selling cheap "strange meat" drove them out of business. Ben suspected the rival vendor was selling human flesh, a belief that appeared validated when the vendor went insane, died, and human remains were later found in their crawlspace. Ben eventually earned enough caps to buy a passport into the New Vegas Strip, where he worked as a crier at The Tops casino and was given a casino apartment. He was framed for stealing from the casino vault and was fired, losing his apartment and returning to Freeside.

Old Lady Gibson, often called simply Gibson, runs a scrap yard north of Novac. A lifelong scavenger, she traveled with caravans in her youth and became acquainted with Doctor Henry during those years. She later settled near Novac with her husband, and together they spent much of their lives scavenging the REPCONN Test Site for salvage to sell. After her husband's death, she continues to operate the scrapyard, offering repair services and selling various items.

Papa Khan is the chief and leader of the Great Khans, a raider tribe based in Red Rock Canyon. He resides in the Great Khan Longhouse, the only concrete building in the village, and is described by at least one acquaintance as a softie at heart despite the fearsome reputation of his people. Papa Khan has entered into an alliance with Caesar's Legion, guided by the Legion's envoy Karl, though he fails to recognize the danger this partnership poses to his tribe. His desire to leave a legacy of greatness and seek revenge against the NCR for past conflicts heavily influences his leadership decisions.

Philippe is the executive chef of the Gourmand restaurant at the Ultra-Luxe casino in New Vegas, serving the White Glove Society. He is renowned for elevating brahmin steak into a delicacy and considers himself the god of New Vegas brahmin fusion cuisine. Philippe has an intense obsession with fresh ingredients and a notoriously volatile temper, likely rooted in a traumatic childhood involving an absent father, a chem-addicted mother, and abusive siblings who would lock him in a shipping crate. He has spent considerable effort experimenting with substitutes to approximate the taste of human flesh, keeping handwritten recipes of his various attempts, with his "Sweet Veal" recipe undergoing the most revisions.

Private Davey Crenshaw is an NCR soldier stationed at Camp McCarran, widely regarded as a disciplinary problem and prankster with no regard for those around him. His antics, such as leading a brahmin upstairs in the terminal building and destroying toilets with firecrackers, have made him unpopular among his fellow troopers, though he remains unrepentant and considers his reputation a point of pride. He has also sabotaged computer security and hacked terminals for mischief, prompting personnel to be more mindful of their terminals. Due to his conduct and his superiors' lack of faith in him, he was assigned to guard a remote post at the camp.

Ranger Andy is a former NCR Ranger who serves as Novac's closest thing to a lawman, watching over the town while others monitor the highway. He was forced into retirement years ago after a raid on Legion slavers went wrong, when a child hiding in a closet left a live grenade at his feet, mangling half his body and leaving him with lasting damage to his arm and leg. He settled in Novac and took on a informal sheriff role, known for having a good eye for people and being one of the few residents who didn't dislike Carla Boone, viewing her directness as a coping mechanism for frontier life. He stays in touch with active Rangers at Ranger Station Charlie through his ham radio, with patrols checking on him regularly.

Ranger Dobson is an NCR Ranger originally from Redding who has seen extensive action against slavers during his career. As of 2281, he is stationed at Camp McCarran but has gone off on his own to scout the NCR Correctional Facility lost to the Powder Gangers, setting up a safehouse in a Hidden Valley bunker. His primary target is the terrorist Samuel Cooke and his gang of roamers, whom he considers the most dangerous of the Powder Gangers, though he despises all of them for preying on caravans and civilians and will shoot any on sight. Dobson is confident and takes pride in protecting the innocent of the Mojave Wasteland, but knows his limits and loves to joke around with anyone, even radio operators at McCarran HQ, which has led them to take his reports less seriously.

Ranger Ghost is an NCR Ranger stationed at the Mojave Outpost, where she serves as a marksman defending against threats approaching from the I-15. She is frustrated with her assignment and the state of the NCR under President Kimball, viewing the outpost as a bureaucratic dead end. She is concerned about a lack of traffic and smoke rising from the nearby town of Nipton, which she suspects may be the result of an attack by Powder Gangers. She is perceptive in reading people and can determine a person's trade by their walking pattern.

Ranger Jackson is an NCR Ranger serving as the commanding officer of Mojave Outpost, where he maintains a standing force in accordance with his orders. He would prefer less bureaucracy and more direct results in the ongoing conflict, but arriving reinforcements are routed to Camp McCarran and frontline outposts like Camp Forlorn Hope, leaving him unable to send patrols to protect caravans that come under attack. While he cannot officially hire mercenaries, he is known to lose supplies to individuals willing to take on dangerous assignments, such as clearing routes through the Ivanpah valley so caravan traffic can resume. Cass, who trusts him enough to ask him to bring her case forward to the relevant NCR institutions, refers to him as a washed-out old fuckup who has served long enough to only see the worst outcome of everything.

Raul Alfonso Tejada is a ghoul mechanic and former gunslinger born in 2047 who was living at Hidalgo Ranch outside Mexico City before the Great War. After losing most of his family to refugees who burned their home, he fled with his younger sister Rafaela to the radioactive ruins of Mexico City, where he began ghoulifying from radiation exposure. Rafaela was killed by raiders, prompting Raul to hunt down and kill those responsible. He eventually made his way to Tucson, Arizona, known locally as Two-Sun, where he lived for 75 years under the name Miguel and watched over a prostitute named Claudia who resembled his late sister, only to lose her as well to a gang led by Dirty Dave.

Rex, often called Rexie by The King, is a cyberdog living in Freeside as the loyal companion of the man himself. A Mk. III Support Model, he served as a police dog in Colorado before the Great War and later saw combat duty with Caesar's Legion, a past he still retains memories of. The King obtained him from a salvager a few years ago and had the Followers of the Apocalypse repair his battered, scorched bodywork.

Robert Edwin House, commonly known as Mr. House, is the founder of RobCo Industries and the sole proprietor of the New Vegas Strip as of 2281. Before the Great War, he predicted the nuclear apocalypse and integrated himself into a life-extension chamber within the Lucky 38 casino to oversee the city's missile defense. Although the loss of the Platinum Chip caused him to fall into a decades-long coma, he awoke to recruit local tribes into the Three Families and establish New Vegas before the New California Republic could claim it.

Sergeant Bitter-Root is a sniper serving with Alpha Team of the NCR First Recon at Camp McCarran. Born to Great Khan parents at Bitter Springs, he endured a grim childhood with a sadistic, alcoholic father who took him killing NCR personnel and civilians from age three, and a mother who repeatedly tried to sell him into slavery for jet. He was liberated during the Bitter Springs Massacre by then-Captain Major Dhatri, who took him in as his son. Bitter-Root chose his name as part of a Great Khans naming tradition, referring both to his bitter upbringing and the massacre he considers his rite of passage.

Sergeant Daniel Contreras is the head of the Camp McCarran Supply Shack and a supply merchant for the NCR Army. He uses his position to steal weapons and ammunition meant for military use and resell them on the black market to mercenaries, employing intermediaries to keep his hands clean and the military police off his trail. Lieutenant Carrie Boyd suspects him of wrongdoing, but despite weekly inventory checks coming up short on guns and ammo, Contreras always pawns off the goods before the MPs can search his possessions and quarters. He also uses his connections to acquire chemical components intended for Army medical use that can be used to manufacture potent recreational drugs, and his Westside contact named Price is already in custody, making it only a matter of time before authorities arrest the sergeant for chem trafficking.

Silus is a centurion of Caesar's Legion who was captured by the NCR during battle and brought to Camp McCarran for interrogation. Unlike most Legionaries, he retained independent thought despite indoctrination, and his intelligence and critical observation set him apart. He earned his rank through years of devoted service and bravery, once charging armed men with nothing but a knife. However, after delaying a time-critical mission for three days while waiting for Caesar's headache to subside, his centuria was ambushed and routed by the NCR.

Tech Sergeant Reyes manages radio communications at Camp Forlorn Hope, compiling reports from Ranger stations and Camp McCarran. She discovered alarming inconsistencies in enemy sighting reports and suspects compromised codes, but her superiors dismiss her concerns, viewing her as an incompetent desk jockey. She seeks help to verify radio security with Ranger stations to pinpoint interference affecting the NCR's war effort.

The Forecaster is a young orphaned boy living beneath the 188 Trading Post overpass in the Mojave Wasteland. He possesses psychic abilities that allow him to provide insights into both the past and future, which he shares with travelers in exchange for caps. To manage the severe headaches caused by overusing his powers, he wears a Psychic Nullifier he calls his "medicine," though it also blanks his mind. He surrounds himself with collected wasteland items like books, cameras, and flags to cope with the emptiness.

Thomas Hildern is the director of the Office of Science and Industry (OSI) eastern division, operating out of Camp McCarran's Terminal Building. Educated by the Followers of the Apocalypse, he parted ways with them over their adherence to old-world dogma, preferring to focus on large-scale results. He helped form OSI, an organization dedicated to finding practical applications for knowledge. As director of the eastern division, his team oversees the optimization of Hoover Dam power output and research into advancing food production, including supervision of the NCR Sharecropper Farms initiative.

Ulysses is a courier and former Frumentarii of Caesar's Legion, originally from the Twisted Hairs tribe of Arizona. After Caesar betrayed his tribe and enslaved its members at Dry Wells, Ulysses continued to serve the Legion as a scout before settling in Hopeville, which was destroyed by nuclear missiles triggered by a package delivered by another courier. He survived the destruction and blamed the Courier for the loss of his home, seeking answers and revenge. Ulysses traveled to Big MT, where the Think Tank explained to him how the Divide's missiles were activated, and he later aided the White Legs tribe in their campaign against New Canaan on Caesar's orders.

Veronica is a Brotherhood of Steel Scribe assigned to the Mojave chapter, operating out of the Hidden Valley Bunker and frequently visiting the 188 Trading Post to trade and scavenge. She traveled to the Mojave as a child with her parents under Father Elijah's leadership, originally bound for Hoover Dam before Elijah diverted the group to occupy HELIOS One instead. Both of her parents were killed fighting the New California Republic, after which Elijah became her mentor and guardian, nurturing her fascination with technology. She was away from HELIOS One when the NCR seized it, and the survivors retreated underground under Elder McNamara's permanent lockdown, a policy Veronica openly opposed out of fear that isolationism would doom the Brotherhood to extinction.

Yes Man is a reprogrammed PDQ-88b securitron that serves as Benny's assistant in New Vegas. Originally a standard securitron working for Mr. House, he was damaged by a pulse grenade and recovered by Benny, who had Followers of the Apocalypse member Emily Ortal reprogram him. The reprogramming made Yes Man incapable of refusing any order or withholding information from anyone, making his name a literal job description. Benny intended to install Yes Man's AI onto the Lucky 38 mainframe to seize control of all securitrons on the Strip.
